Atlanta Plant Manager
CITGO
Atlanta, GA
Citgo Petroleum Corporation
CITGO Petroleum Corporation is a recognized leader in the refining industry and operates under the well-known CITGO brand. CITGO owns and operates three refineries located in Lake Charles, LA.; Lemont, IL.; and Corpus Christi, TX, and wholly and/or jointly owns 43 active terminals, nine pipelines and three lubricants blending and packaging plants. With approximately 3,300 employees and a combined crude capacity of approximately 829,000 barrels-per-day (bpd), positions CITGO as one of the best-branded supplier companies in the industry.
At CITGO our people are our most important resource. Our core values are Safety, Integrity, Respect, Accountability, and Care.
Job duties displayed above are not all-inclusive, site-specific responsibilities may be assigned.
Here are the incentives we offer:
Remote Work options available for eligible positions
Options are department and/or location specific
9/80 Work Schedule Option (where applicable)
Annual Vacation Incentive (40-120 hours of additional pay) for Eligible Employees
Paid Vacation Time
Company-Paid Holidays
Caregiver Leave
Excellent 401(k) Match
Pension Plan
Performance Incentive
Company-Paid Sick Leave and Long-Term Disability
Medical, Dental, & Vision Plans; FSA and HSA options
Company-Paid Life Insurance for Active Employees
Healthy Rewards Program
Service Awards Program
Educational Assistance Plan
Dependent Children Scholarships
Reimbursement for Gym Membership
Employee Discount Programs
On-site Health Clinic (select locations)
On-site Cafeteria (select locations)
On-site Credit Union and ATM (Corporate office only)
On-site Fitness Center (select locations)
PLEASE NOTE ALL JOBS DO NOT QUALIFY FOR ALL PERKS
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.
Requisition ID - 2244
Job Summary
Manage the complete operation of the Atlanta Lubricant Manufacturing Facility to ensure maximum efficiency of blending, packaging and customer fulfillment processes. Direct the manufacturing of products and control the inventory of finished products, raw materials including base oils, additives and containers as the MRP controller. Control and direct facility staffing and organization plan. Responsible for achieving and maintaining safety, environmental, health and training goals. Responsible for implementing accounting and inventory control programs. Manage the corporate relationship with the local community and various government agencies. Establish and execute facility long range plan, expenses, capital and staffing budgets. Develop major plant improvements. Make recommendations on new business opportunities for the facility as well as the lubricants business in general.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Engineering or related field plus 8 years manufacturing experience OR 12 years of lubricant manufacturing experience if no Bachelor's Degree.
Job Duties
Safety and Compliance: Ensuring a safe working environment is a top priority. Plant managers implement safety training programs, enforce OSHA and environmental regulations, conduct audits, and investigate incidents to prevent future hazards. Ensure proper use of personal protective equipment and adherence to hazard communication standards.2. Operational Oversight: Plant managers coordinate daily operations, including production scheduling, workflow monitoring, and inventory control, to ensure that manufacturing objectives are met efficiently and cost-effectively. Manage the flow of materials, labor utilization, and equipment to maintain production levels and quality standards.
Leadership and Team Development: Hiring, training, mentoring, and evaluating staff are key responsibilities. Plant managers set performance expectations, conduct reviews, resolve conflicts, and foster teamwork and accountability across departments.
Budget and Cost Management: Plant managers prepare and monitor budgets, control operating expenditures, and implement cost-effective systems for labor, wages, and maintenance. Make strategic decisions regarding staffing, equipment, and resource allocation to optimize financial performance.
Job Duties II
Strategic Planning: Beyond daily operations, plant managers collaborate with corporate leadership to align plant capabilities with business goals, evaluate new technologies, scale capacity, and plan long-term improvements They analyze KPIs and production data to identify trends and implement continuous improvement initiatives.
Maintenance and Equipment Management: Plant managers oversee maintenance schedules, ensure machinery reliability, and coordinate preventive maintenance to minimize downtime.
Project management: Direct Plant projects to keep them on schedule in Budget and safely completed. May also manage capital assets and approve production schedules to maintain operational efficiency.
Communication and Coordination: facilitate cross-department collaboration, lead production meetings, report performance metrics to stakeholders, and ensure smooth coordination between production, maintenance, supply chain, and quality control teams.
All Qualified Candidate Can Apply @ careers.citgo.com﻿

Plant Manager
MOBIS Corporate Center of America
Blythewood, SC
The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and operational performance of the Mobis South Carolina Electrified Powertrain (MSCe) manufacturing facility. This role directs and coordinates plant operations, including Production, Quality, Production Control & Material Management (PCMM), Logistics, and Maintenance, to achieve company objectives related to Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Morale (SQDCM).
The Plant Manager serves as the senior operational leader of the facility and is accountable for plant readiness, launch execution, production ramp-up, operational excellence, customer satisfaction, and long term business growth. This position provides both strategic and day-to-day operational leadership to ensure the successful achievement of startup, equipment installation and commissioning, pilot production, Start of Production (SOP), capacity expansion, and customer delivery objectives.
The Plant Manager acts as the primary plant representative for customer visits, operational reviews,
business discussions, audits, and performance escalation matters while maintaining close collaboration with Headquarters, MCCA, customers, suppliers, and regulatory agencies. As a key member of the site leadership team, the incumbent drives cross-functional alignment, organizational development, and continuous improvement across manufacturing operations.
Responsibilities
(To perform successfully in this position, the incumbent must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Other duties may be assigned.)
Plant Operations Leadership
Lead and oversee all manufacturing operations to achieve company goals, production targets, and customer requirements.
Develop and implement operational strategies supporting plant startup, production ramp-up, capacity expansion, and long-term growth.
Lead plant readiness, launch management, equipment installation, commissioning, pilot production, SOP, and production ramp-up activities.
Establish and monitor key operational metrics, including Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Morale, and Productivity.
Drive cross-functional problem solving and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance plant performance.
Ensure compliance with MOBIS policies, customer requirements, and applicable laws and
regulations.
Act as the primary plant representative for customer visits, operational reviews, performance escalations, and strategic discussions.
Production Management
Direct all production activities to achieve production schedules, capacity targets, product quality requirements, and customer delivery commitments.
Optimize manufacturing resources, manpower planning, line balancing, equipment utilization, throughput, and overall operational effectiveness.
Lead production readiness for new programs and support process validation, trial builds, pilot production, and manufacturing process improvements.
Coordinate cross-functional activities to resolve operational issues, remove launch constraints, and ensure stable production performance.
Quality Leadership
Ensure compliance with the quality management system, customer-specific requirements, and applicable automotive industry standards.
Lead quality improvement initiatives and foster a culture of defect prevention, accountability, and continuous quality excellence.
Oversee customer quality performance, corrective actions, root cause investigations, containment activities, and audit readiness.
Support the implementation and maintenance of quality systems and processes aligned with IATF 16949, VDA requirements, and applicable OEM customer-specific requirements.
Production Control, Material Management & Logistics
Oversee production planning, material planning, inventory control, warehousing, and logistics operations.
Ensure uninterrupted and timely material availability to support launch and production requirements.
Monitor inventory accuracy, material flow efficiency, warehouse performance, and on-time delivery results.
Coordinate supply chain activities with customers, suppliers, and internal teams to achieve delivery, inventory, and production objectives.
Maintenance & Facility Readiness
Oversee maintenance programs to ensure equipment reliability, uptime, preventive maintenance effectiveness, and operational readiness.
Lead maintenance readiness for equipment installation, commissioning, trial production, SOP, and production ramp-up.
Promote safe operating practices and coordinate with the responsible EHS function to support compliance, incident prevention, and corrective actions.
Support facility readiness, utility availability, infrastructure improvements, and technical issue resolution required for plant operations.
Customer Management
Serve as the senior plant contact for OEM customers regarding plant performance, launch status, delivery, quality, capacity, and operational concerns.
Lead preparation for customer visits, audits, operational reviews, business meetings, and escalation discussions.
Ensure timely cross-functional response to customer concerns and oversee implementation of sustainable corrective actions.
Maintain effective customer relationships and align plant priorities with customer expectations and business commitments.
Organizational Leadership & Profitability Management
Manage plant operating budgets, capital expenditures (CAPEX), cost improvement initiatives, and overall plant financial performance.
Drive productivity, cost reduction, waste elimination, and profitability improvement while protecting safety, quality, and delivery performance.
Develop department leaders and support workforce planning, succession planning, organizational capability, and employee engagement.
Collaborate with Business Administration and executive leadership to achieve operational, financial, and strategic business objectives.
AUTHORITY & SCOPE
This position is responsible for the overall management and operational performance of MSCe
manufacturing operations, including Production, Quality, Production Control & Material Management (PCMM), Logistics, and Maintenance. The incumbent exercises independent judgment in plant operations, launch execution, production planning, resource allocation, cost and profitability management, quality performance, customer response, and operational improvement initiatives within approved company guidelines. The position partners closely with executive leadership, Headquarters, MCCA, customers, suppliers, and regulatory agencies to achieve business objectives and operational excellence.
Matters involving significant financial impact, strategic business decisions, legal risks, major
organizational changes, or significant customer escalations are reviewed with executive leadership as appropriate.
Supervisory Responsibilities:
Yes, Directly oversees department leaders responsible for Production, Maintenance, Quality, Production Control & Material Management (PCMM), and Logistics. Provides strategic leadership and operational direction across all manufacturing functions, ensuring alignment with business objectives while driving operational excellence, employee development, accountability, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.
QUALIFICATIONS
(The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required and preferred for this position.)
Required Education & Experience:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Business Management, or a related field.
Minimum 15 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including at least 7 years of leadership experience in automotive manufacturing operations.
Demonstrated experience leading plant startup, greenfield launch, equipment installation and commissioning, pilot production, SOP, or production ramp-up activities.
Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Strong knowledge of automotive manufacturing operations, production systems, launch management, and operational excellence methodologies.
Thorough understanding of automotive quality standards and core tools, including IATF 16949, APQP, PPAP, FMEA, SPC, and MSA.
Working knowledge of VDA requirements and OEM customer-specific requirements applicable to the assigned business.
Strong knowledge of production planning, material management, inventory control, logistics, and supply chain operations.
Knowledge of maintenance management, equipment reliability, preventive maintenance, and manufacturing facility readiness.
Understanding of OSHA requirements and the ability to partner effectively with the responsible EHS function to support a safe and compliant workplace.
Proven ability to lead large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations and drive measurable operational performance.
Strong leadership, coaching, employee development, succession planning, and organizational management skills.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, presentation, negotiation, customer management, and stakeholder management abilities.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, escalation management, and decision-making capabilities.
Experience managing operating budgets, cost reduction initiatives, capital investments, profitability, and business planning activities.
Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on operational execution in a fast-paced startup and manufacturing environment.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, and experience with manufacturing reporting systems.
Preferred Education & Experience
Experience in automotive, electric vehicle (EV), battery, electrified powertrain, or advanced manufacturing environments.
Experience leading a greenfield project, startup plant, major plant launch, or capacity expansion.
Experience overseeing Production, Quality, Production Control & Material Management, Logistics, and Maintenance functions.
Experience working within a global manufacturing organization and matrix reporting structure.
Experience supporting OEM customer requirements, customer audits, launch reviews, and performance escalations.
Experience coordinating with Headquarters, regional leadership teams, suppliers, customers, and regulatory agencies.
Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement leadership experience preferred.
Certificates, Licenses & Registrations
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent Continuous Improvement certification preferred.
Working Conditions:
Manufacturing plant environment with routine presence on the production floor and frequent interaction with Production, Quality, Maintenance, Logistics, and administrative personnel.
The incumbent is expected to regularly support plant readiness activities, equipment installation and commissioning, pilot production, SOP preparation, production operations, customer visits, audits, operational reviews, continuous improvement initiatives, and capacity expansion activities at the MSCe manufacturing facility.
Occasional domestic and international travel may be required for training, customer meetings,
benchmarking activities, business reviews, supplier visits, and coordination with Headquarters, MCCA, customers, and other MOBIS operations. The position may require extended working hours during plant startup, production ramp-up, major operational events, customer support activities, audits, or other business-critical situations.

evidence.quote: 7+ years of experience in hardware production, manufacturing, or complex system assembly
evidence.text:
Robotics Head of Production
Cleo Robotics
Boston, MA
Full-time, exempt
Boston, Massachusetts
On-site, five days per week
Reports to the CEO
About Us
Cleo Robotics builds unconventional autonomous robotic systems designed to operate in the world’s most challenging and inaccessible environments. Our mission is to deploy intelligent machines into critical environments to improve operational efficiency, reduce unplanned downtime, and keep people out of harm’s way. Our technology is used across industries including energy, oil and gas, manufacturing, public safety, and defense. We’re a growing team of experts in robotics and autonomous systems with diverse backgrounds and skills. We value making an impact, thinking big, leading with empathy, and having fun along the way.
If you get excited about solving big problems and building robots straight from science fiction, and you thrive in a fast-paced environment, this role might be for you!
About The Role
Cleo Robotics is seeking a Head of Production to build our production function from the ground up. This is a foundational, first-of-its-kind role responsible for transforming our current small batch builds into scalable production.
You will begin as a hands-on builder, working directly on assembly while owning production strategy, supplier development, and team building.You will own production end-to-end — from first build to scaled manufacturing — including output, quality, cost, and delivery.
In the early stages, you will spend a significant portion of your time personally executing core production work (assembly, testing, inventory, fulfillment), while simultaneously designing the systems, infrastructure, and processes that will enable scale.
As production grows, you will transition from being the primary builder to hiring and leading a production team — shifting your focus toward oversight, process optimization, and team leadership, while remaining close enough to the hardware to guide builds, train team members, and uphold quality standards.
What You’ll Do
Product Build
Initially act as the primary individual contributor responsible for building and validating systems, while establishing the standards that future team members will follow
Assemble full drone systems and subassemblies with high precision and repeatability
Perform soldering, wiring, integration, calibration, and system bring-up
Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair hardware systems
Support prototype builds and engineering iterations
Establish “gold standard” builds for future production replication
Ensure every system shipped meets performance and reliability standards
Production Build-Out & Scale-Up
Design and implement the production function from scratch
Define and implement the end-to-end production workflow (build → test → ship)
Design production floor layout, tooling, and workstations
Establish assembly line processes and throughput models
Create scalable systems for:
Work instructions
Quality control checkpoints
Build tracking and traceability
Transition from prototype builds → low-rate production → scalable manufacturing
Introduce and implement lean manufacturing principles
Documentation & Process Infrastructure
Turn tribal knowledge into scalable systems
Create and maintain:
Assembly guides
Standard operating procedures (SOPs)
Test and calibration protocols
Implement version control for production documentation
Ensure processes are clear, repeatable, and transferable to new hires
Quality Systems & Reliability
Ensure production quality scales with the business
Define and enforce quality control standards and testing procedures
Build inspection, validation, and failure analysis processes
Track production metrics (yield, defects, rework rates)
Implement continuous improvement loops
Partner with engineering to improve reliability and manufacturability
Production Planning & Execution
Own delivery timelines and output
Build and manage production schedules
Align builds with customer demand and internal priorities
Identify bottlenecks and proactively resolve them
Ensure on-time delivery of production units
Drive throughput, yield, and cost efficiency
Track and improve key production metrics
Inventory, Fulfillment & Operations
Build the operational backbone of production
Own inventory management systems
Own demand planning and material forecasting
Manage receiving, storage, and part traceability
Oversee shipping, logistics, and fulfillment operations
Ensure production readiness at all times (tools, materials, workspace)
Vendor & Supply Chain Management
Own supplier relationships and hardware sourcing strategy
Identify, onboard, and manage suppliers and contract manufacturers
Negotiate pricing, lead times, and supply agreements
Ensure component quality, reliability, and availability
Develop redundancy and risk mitigation strategies in the supply chain
Manage inbound logistics and supplier performance
Collaborate with engineering on design-for-manufacturing (DFM) decisions
Team Building & Leadership
Own the transition of day-to-day build execution to the team you hire, while maintaining accountability for output, quality, and delivery
Hire and train production technicians and specialists
Define roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations
Build a culture of quality, ownership, and craftsmanship
Act as the bridge between engineering and operations
What You Bring
7+ years of experience in hardware production, manufacturing, or complex system assembly
Experience in 0→1 or early-stage production environments (robotics, drones, aerospace, hardware startups)
Strong hands-on builder with the ability to assemble and troubleshoot systems directly
Equally comfortable at the workbench and at the system level
Advanced experience with:
Electronics assembly, soldering, wiring, PCBs
Mechanical assembly and integration
Strong understanding of:
Production workflows
Supply chain and vendor management
Inventory systems and logistics
Experience implementing:
Manufacturing processes
Quality systems
Production scaling strategies
BONUS POINTS
Experience scaling production from prototype → manufacturing
Background in drones, robotics, aerospace, or defense hardware
You don’t want to inherit a production system, you want to build it
What We Offer
The opportunity to build autonomy that moves beyond simulation and operates on real robots in challenging, mission-critical environments
Meaningful ownership of a core product capability, with the ability to influence Cleo’s autonomy architecture, technical direction, and roadmap
A high-impact role on a small, talented team where your ideas can move rapidly from development to real-world deployment
The opportunity to expand your technical scope, take on greater ownership, and grow alongside the company
Competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package, including health, dental, and vision insurance
Equity for every new hire, giving everyone the opportunity to share in Cleo’s growth
Flexible paid time off and company holidays
A collaborative, energetic workplace with a fully stocked kitchen and regular team gatherings

Vice President, Quality
Sabin Vaccine Institute
United States
Description
Department:
Research & Development (R&D)
Reports to:
President, R&D
Location:
Remote Work, US only
Why Sabin
Our mission is to make vaccines more accessible, enable innovation, and expand immunization across the globe. We seek a future free from vaccine-preventable diseases. We are an innovative, collaborative, and engaged team that values accountability, teamwork, partnership, and driving impact. We are vaccine champions improving lives through immunization. Sabin staff, management, and the Board of Trustees are committed to ensuring that fairness, integrity, and opportunity remain at the core of how we operate.
Position Summary
At Sabin, R&D is focused on advancing vaccines through development and addressing unmet needs. The Vice President, Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for GxP quality across Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP), and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP).
This role builds and sustains a phase-appropriate Quality Management System (QMS) for a virtual nonprofit organization, ensuring that development activities remain integrated, risk-based, data-driven, compliant, and inspection-ready as programs advance through late-stage development, outbreak-response and emergency-use readiness, Process Performance Qualification (PPQ), Phase 3 clinical trials, regulatory submissions, inspections, licensure, and commercial readiness.
The Vice President establishes and oversees a scalable sponsor oversight model that defines decision rights, delegated responsibilities, quality agreements, governance forums, performance expectations, escalation pathways, and records-access requirements across internal teams and a global network of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, consultants, and other critical partners. The role balances regulatory obligations, program timelines, organizational capacity, and mission-driven priorities.
As a member of the R&D Leadership Team, the Vice President establishes quality strategy and governance, strengthens quality culture, advises executive leadership, and builds a high-performing Quality organization. This position serves as Sabin’s primary authority on GxP compliance, quality risk management, and inspection readiness.
Responsibilities
Develop and execute a roadmap for evolving the current mid-stage clinical phase-appropriate QMS into a mature QMS spanning GMP, GCP, GVP, and GLP to support advanced development activities, licensure-enabling regulatory submissions and inspections, and commercial readiness.
Serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership on quality, compliance, inspection readiness, and risk management.
Embed quality culture across functions, partners, and development programs and strengthen organizational capabilities for increasing regulatory complexity.
Own quality governance, metrics, escalation pathways, management review, and quality risk management frameworks.
Provide senior leadership, guidance, and direction for:
GMP quality activities supporting vaccine development, technology transfer, process validation, PPQ, commercial readiness, and lifecycle management.
GCP quality systems supporting clinical development, including audit programs, inspection readiness, vendor oversight, and quality risk management.
GVP quality activities supporting pharmacovigilance throughout clinical development and post-authorization, including adverse-event reporting, signal management, aggregate safety reporting, and regulatory compliance.
GLP-related quality activities supporting nonclinical studies, including pivotal nonhuman primate studies.
Establish and approve quality agreements and oversee risk-based qualification, auditing, monitoring, and periodic requalification of CDMOs, CROs, laboratories, depots, and other GxP partners. Ensure clear responsibilities, escalation and reporting requirements, audit and data-access rights, change and deviation notification, CAPA management, inspection support, and remediation.
Provide quality oversight for validated GxP systems, document and data governance, records retention, data integrity, and remote-inspection capabilities. Partner with IT to support cybersecurity and business-continuity requirements for GxP systems.
Lead inspection readiness and serve as the sponsor quality lead for FDA Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO), Pre-Approval Inspections (PAIs), surveillance inspections, and other health authority inspections, including inspection logistics, subject-matter expert preparation, document production, response strategy, and closure of regulatory commitments.
Direct critical investigations involving serious breaches, significant safety or data-integrity concerns, material manufacturing deviations, or systemic quality failures, ensuring timely containment, root-cause analysis, regulatory assessment, and sustainable corrective and preventive action (CAPA).
Ensure quality systems and GxP documentation are complete, controlled, inspection-ready, and aligned with applicable FDA, EMA, ICH, WHO, and other regulatory expectations.
Identify and escalate quality risks, drive timely mitigation, and support alignment with internal stakeholders and funding partners.
Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing Quality professionals.
Provide strategic oversight and contribute to required quality content for Investigational New Drug applications (INDs), Biologics License Applications (BLAs), Marketing Authorization Applications (MAAs), responses to health authority information requests, and other associated regulatory submissions.
Provide Quality leadership for funding proposals and due-diligence activities.
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant scientific, engineering, quality, or related field and at least 16 years of progressively responsible quality experience in biologics development and manufacturing; an advanced degree is preferred. Experience with vaccines, viral vectors, or similarly complex biologics is strongly preferred.
Proven people-leadership experience and success driving organizational change, preferably in a small biotechnology and/or virtual organization. Experience serving on an R&D or executive leadership team is preferred.
Demonstrated success developing or substantially transforming a QMS in preparation for late-stage development and licensure.
Direct experience supporting late-stage clinical development, process validation, PPQ, PAI readiness, and BLA/MAA submissions.
Experience leading health authority inspections and interacting with FDA and other global regulatory agencies.
Expert knowledge of GMP, GCP, GLP, and GVP requirements; relevant ICH guidelines, including ICH E6(R3), E8, E9, Q9, and Q10; and applicable FDA, EMA, MHRA, WHO, and other global regulatory expectations.
Demonstrated experience establishing sponsor oversight and quality governance across outsourced development and manufacturing networks, including CDMOs, CROs, and contract laboratories.
Broad understanding of the interdependencies among nonclinical development, translational science, Phase 3 clinical operations, pharmacovigilance, biostatistics and data management, CMC, regulatory strategy, and quality, with the ability to identify and mitigate cross-functional risks to licensure.
Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively across technical functions, external partners, geographic regions, and matrixed teams, with strong judgment, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills.
Experience supporting U.S. government-funded projects is preferred.
Other
Must demonstrate interest in furthering Sabin’s mission.
Subject to a criminal background investigation.
Request for three professional references.
Verification of education/degrees.
Work Authorization
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship.
Compensation And Benefits
Sabin’s philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased, equitable, competitive compensation and benefits. Using benchmarking and salary survey data, the annual salary for this position is up to $315,000. The exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, training, and certifications/degree. As a grant-funded organization, Sabin actively seeks funding for existing and new programs.
Sabin provides a comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees, featuring medical, dental, and vision coverage as well as flexible spending accounts. Eligible employees enjoy flexible vacation leave, sick leave, and both short-term and long-term disability options. The organization observes 10 federal holidays plus an end-of-year winter break. Additionally, Sabin offers an employer matching 401(k) plan.
Notice to Recruiters/Staffing Agencies
Recruitment vendors may not contact Sabin hiring managers, executives, or employees and must have an executed agreement on file. Unsolicited resumes do not create an agreement, and Sabin is not responsible for related fees.
Sabin is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to their race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, disability or genetic information, sex (including gender identity, pregnancy or sexual orientation), marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

This is a highly visible role at the site and Division level and, as a key member of the leadership team, you will report to the CDD Vice President, Global Quality Assurance & Regulatory Affairs.
A critical aspect of this role is serving as the primary quality representative for customers and regulatory authorities. As the site's Management Representative, the Director is responsible for ensuring the effectiveness of the Quality Management System and leading interactions during FDA inspections, MDSAP and ISO 13485 audits, and customer audits. This role requires strong leadership and communication skills to build customer confidence, maintain regulatory compliance, and represent Thermo Fisher Scientific with credibility and professionalism.
Key Responsibilities:
Acts as Management Representative of the Quality System and official correspondent of the site to all regulators (including US FDA). Primary contact at the site for all audits (regulator, Notified Body and customer).
Serve as a member of the site leadership team, providing strategic direction and influencing business decisions to ensure quality, compliance, and operational excellence are integrated into site objectives.
Establish strategies and drives actions to ensure the Quality Management System is adequate and successfully implemented to remain in sustained compliance with applicable regulations and standards.
Responsible for site product quality, compliance, conformance to quality requirements and specifications, and customer quality requirements. Supports regulatory recalls and interaction with government agencies.
Directly interacts with customers and OEM partners in relation to quality agreements, and quality matters associated with provided products and services.
Champion risk-based decision making by overseeing quality risk management processes and ensuring risks are identified, assessed, mitigated, and monitored throughout the product lifecycle.
Attracts, develops, and retains top talent to build an outstanding quality / regulatory function. Implements the required interpersonal structures and operating mechanisms to maintain appropriate oversight of the compliance status of the business and achieve results.
Grows and develops a customer-focused culture of personal quality in all site functions through leading, educating, and motivating site personnel using industry-leading practices.
Establishes and leads annual personnel resource and financial plans for the quality / regulatory organization.
Establishes annual site quality goals and objectives as part of annual Quality Improvement Plan and develops strategies and tactics to deliver associated results.
Leads and participates in cross functional teams for new product development, technology transfer, process improvement, and general operations.
Partners with regulatory affairs in all aspects of site regulatory processes that ensure the appropriate licensing, marketing and legal compliance of all appropriate diagnostics and medical device products globally.
Collaborate with global Quality and Regulatory leadership to standardize best practices, share lessons learned, and support enterprise quality initiatives.
Minimum Requirements/Qualifications:
A minimum of 10 years of quality / regulatory experience including at least 5 years of prior experience leading a quality / regulatory role.
Undergraduate degree in life science or biomedical engineering-related subject area preferred.
Strong demonstration of leadership capabilities required, with experience in driving organization and process change. Experience in leading transformations is preferred.
Strong solid understanding of QMS standards and medical device requirements/regulations (ISO 13485:2016 (preferably under MDSAP), US FDA QMSR, Health Canada, IVDD / IVDR)
Experienced in direct, professional interactions with customers and OEM business partners and regulatory authorities.
Ability to achieve results in a matrixed organization, using representatives from diverse cultures and embracing diversity.
Travel requirement:
<10% regional and international travel is expected.
Compensation And Benefits
The salary range estimated for this position based in Virginia is $145,500.00–$225,000.00.
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount
For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

evidence.text:
Senior Director, Test & Product Engineering
No longer accepting applications
Renesas Electronics
Austin, TX
The Senior Director of Test & Product Engineering leads the strategy and execution of test and product engineering for power semiconductor modules, power ICs, and controllers supporting data center and high-performance applications. This role owns end-to-end product execution across characterization, qualification, yield ramp, test development, and high-volume manufacturing. The leader ensures delivery of scalable, cost-competitive, and high-quality products through strong cross-functional alignment with Design, Product Line, Quality, Reliability, and Operations.
Job Description
The role defines and executes a unified strategy across test and product engineering while leading global teams and establishing scalable processes for new product introduction, yield ramp, and sustaining operations. It requires a balance of strategic leadership and hands-on execution to drive predictable delivery and continuous improvement.
From a product engineering perspective, this leader owns the full product lifecycle, including silicon bring-up, qualification, ramp, and sustaining. Responsibilities include driving yield ramp and improvement, managing excursions, and optimizing product cost through yield, test efficiency, and manufacturing performance. The role ensures manufacturing readiness, production stability, and resolution of yield issues across fab, assembly, and test. It also owns product KPIs, manages change control processes (ECO/PCN), and partners with design teams on design-for-yield, parametric margining, and specification alignment.
From a test engineering standpoint, the role leads development and deployment of wafer sort, final test, and characterization solutions, ensuring strong test coverage while optimizing cost and efficiency. Responsibilities include driving test time reduction, multisite efficiency, and ATE platform standardization to enable scalable high-volume manufacturing.
The leader is accountable for resolving yield excursions, test escapes, and customer returns while partnering with Quality and Reliability teams to ensure robust qualification and mission-profile alignment. This includes establishing monitoring systems and controls to proactively manage risk and maintain alignment between product performance, test limits, and reliability targets.
The role works closely with Operations and manufacturing partners to ensure production readiness, capacity alignment, and continuous improvement across internal and OSAT sites. Strong cross-functional collaboration is required to align with Design, Product Line, and Applications teams on methodologies, cost targets, and customer requirements.
From a business standpoint, the Senior Director owns budget, headcount, and capital planning, while driving performance against key metrics such as yield, cost, quality, and cycle time. The role is also responsible for building a strong organization through hiring, development, and succession planning.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or related field (advanced degree preferred) with 15+ years of semiconductor experience across test and/or product engineering, including leadership of global teams. Strong technical background in power semiconductors (Si, SiC, GaN, modules, or power ICs) and a proven track record in yield ramp, cost optimization, and high-volume manufacturing execution are required. Deep understanding of ATE, characterization, and yield analysis, along with experience driving cross-functional execution across the full product lifecycle, is essential.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with data center power architectures (AC-DC, DC-DC) and familiarity with power module packaging, thermal behavior, and high-current test methods are preferred. Additional strengths include statistical yield analysis, reliability and qualification methodologies, and experience with test automation and data analytics in manufacturing environments.
Key Performance Indicators
Success in this role is measured by yield performance and improvement, cost of test reduction, product cost competitiveness, execution of NPI and ramp schedules, product quality and reliability, and improvements in cycle time and manufacturing efficiency.
What Success Looks Like
Success is defined by consistent product ramps with strong yield, quality, and cost performance, supported by predictable execution from development through production. The organization demonstrates rapid resolution of yield and quality issues and is recognized as a key driver of product competitiveness and customer satisfaction.
Additional Information
Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier
. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.
At Renesas, TAGIE is our culture, grounded in being Transparent, Agile, Global, Innovative, and Entrepreneurial. It shapes how we work, grow and deliver on our purpose together. This collaborative spirit and mindset drive our semiconductor technology to transform industries and impact millions of lives.
We believe in rewarding our employees with a competitive benefits package alongside their salary. More information will be provided during the hiring process.
Are you ready to join our team and shape the future
with us?
Renesas Electronics is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer, committed to supporting diversity and fostering a work environment free of discrimination on the basis of sex, race, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, military status, veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. For more information, please read our Diversity & Inclusion Statement.
Renesas Electronics deals with dual-use technology that is subject to U.S. export controls regulations. Under these regulations it may be necessary for Renesas to obtain U.S. government export license prior to release of technology to certain persons. The decision whether or not to file or pursue an export license application is at the sole discretion of Renesas.

evidence.quote: In addition to the responsibilities below, this position is also responsible for overseeing the management of doctoral candidates; monitoring post-graduate relationships across teams (e.g., performing interviews, signing off on clinical notes); aligning expectations for and making decisions regarding performing and recommending psychological tests and batteries, ensuring understanding across teams; implementing standards for processing referrals and assignments of assessment and/or testing cases; providing expertise on clinical documentation required for patient medical leave; overseeing testing systems; creating workflows; and driving effective review and approval of patient time off work requests to ensure accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
evidence.text:
Sr. Manager MH EPN Quality, Regulatory, and FIC
Kaiser Permanente
Rancho Cordova, CA
Job Summary:
In addition to the responsibilities below, this position is also responsible for overseeing the management of doctoral candidates; monitoring post-graduate relationships across teams (e.g., performing interviews, signing off on clinical notes); aligning expectations for and making decisions regarding performing and recommending psychological tests and batteries, ensuring understanding across teams; implementing standards for processing referrals and assignments of assessment and/or testing cases; providing expertise on clinical documentation required for patient medical leave; overseeing testing systems; creating workflows; and driving effective review and approval of patient time off work requests to ensure accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
Essential Responsibilities:
Creates and advocates for developmental opportunities for others; builds collaborative, cross-functional relationships. Solicits and acts on performance feedback; works with leaders and employees to set goals and provide open feedback and coaching to drive performance improvement. Pursues professional growth; hires, trains, and develops talent for growth opportunities; strategically evaluates talent for succession planning; sets performance management guidelines and expectations across teams / units. Oversees implementation, adapts, and stays up to date with organizational change, challenges, feedback, best practices, processes, and industry trends; shares best practices within and across teams. Fosters open dialogue amongst team members, engages, motivates, and promotes collaboration within and across teams; motivates teams to meet business objectives. Delegates tasks and decisions as appropriate; provides appropriate support, guidance and scope; encourages development and consideration of options in decision making; fosters access to stakeholders.
Manages designated units or teams by translating business plans into tactical action items; oversees the completion of work assignments and identifies opportunities for improvement; ensures all policies and procedures are followed; partners with key stakeholders and business leaders to ensure products and/or services meet requirements and expectations while aligning with departmental strategies. Aligns team efforts; builds accountability for and measuring progress in achieving results; assumes responsibility for decision making; fosters direct reports to resolve escalated issues as appropriate. Communicates goals and objectives; incorporates resources, costs, and forecasts into team and unit plans; ensures matrixed resources are fulfilling service or performance requirements across reporting lines. Removes obstacles that impact performance; identifies and addresses improvement opportunities; guides performance and develops contingency plans accordingly; influences teams and units to operate in alignment with operational and business objectives.
Manages client care by: providing direction to ensure effective member/patient advocacy as well as implementing customer feedback and/or investigating and resolving member/patient complaints to optimize satisfaction and address care issues; aligning teams on high-quality member/patient care experience and service standards, developing and training teams on standards; and aligning teams on the importance of proper referral of members/patients and developing standards for sharing information with providers.
Manages compliant services by: overseeing daily operations across team to ensure up-to-date compliance with organizational, state, and federal guidelines as well as regulatory policies, standards, and procedures, leading consultations with Compliance; and developing and updating processes to guide teams on written and electronic documentation, records, and reports according to department, federal, and state regulations.
Establishes high quality counseling services by: setting guidelines and expectations for facilitating psychological/behavioral interventions; overseeing communication with patients, members, or families to ensure all team members consistently act with empathy and support when sharing results, discussing treatment plans, providing resources, and answering questions; and developing standards for assessing and treating urgent, high-risk clinical situations (e.g., crisis, suicidal), sharing across teams to guide appropriate interventions and prompt resolutions.
Manages evaluations and diagnoses by: sharing guidelines and coaching teams on member/patient assessments and mental health evaluations, sharing best practices for providing diagnoses and evidence-based treatment plans and approaches for identified diagnoses (e.g., individual and group therapy).
Drives program development and management by: planning and coordinating adjustments to current therapy programs and future program implementation (e.g., in-/out-patient psychotherapy, chemical dependency) or new programs to enhance quality and effectiveness of services; building new systems and processes for outcome management as well as overseeing the implementation of improvements to clinical treatment programs, designs, or protocols; and analyzing the productivity of large, complex therapy programs for providers and ensuring the optimal utilization of programs.

items.title: Plant Manager - Gas Turbine Product Line

evidence.quote: Bachelor’s degree or higher in Engineering, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
evidence.text:
Plant Manager - Gas Turbine Product Line
Siemens Energy
Charlotte, NC
A Snapshot of Your Day
As the Plant Manager for the Gas Turbine manufacturing product line, you will lead all operational activities for a business generating more than $150M in revenue and oversee a team of approximately 200 employees across multiple manufacturing and service operations. You will serve as a key member of the site leadership team, driving performance across safety, quality, people, operational excellence, and growth.
In this role, you'll partner with stakeholders across the business to improve manufacturing performance, reduce lead times, optimize costs, and support long-term strategic objectives. You'll champion lean manufacturing principles while ensuring world-class execution in production, quality, and customer delivery.
How You'll Make An Impact
Lead all operational aspects of the Gas Turbine manufacturing product line, including multiple manufacturing and service centers.
Drive a culture of safety, quality, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Develop and implement lean manufacturing strategies that improve productivity, quality, and cost performance.
Lead, coach, and develop a workforce of approximately 200 employees, including managers, supervisors, professionals, and skilled trades personnel.
Oversee complex manufacturing projects, including planning, execution, resource allocation, and performance management.
Manage organizational budgets, capital investments, new product introductions, and technology implementation initiatives.
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to achieve business objectives and support long-term growth strategies.
What You Bring
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Engineering, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
10 or more years of leadership experience in an industrial or high-volume manufacturing environment.
10 or more years of technical and commercial experience within the power generation industry is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated expertise in lean manufacturing systems and continuous improvement methodologies.
Strong engineering background with hands-on knowledge of machining, welding, advanced assembly, and manufacturing standardization.
Experience with quality management, order management, and customer-facing manufacturing operations.
Deep knowledge of power generation products and manufacturing processes preferred.
Applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States without the need for current or future employer-sponsored work authorization. Siemens Energy employees with current visa sponsorship may be eligible for internal transfers.
About The Team
Gas Services
Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet.
Who is Siemens Energy?
At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: [1] https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo
Rewards
Career growth and development opportunities
Supportive work culture
Company paid Health and wellness benefits
Paid Time Off and paid holidays
401K savings plan with company match
Family building benefits
Parental leave
Jobs & Careers: [2] https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs

Abbott Laboratories

Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.
JOB DESCRIPTION:
Working at Abbott
At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:
Career development with an international company where you can grow the career you dream of.
Employees can qualify for free medical coverage in our Health Investment Plan (HIP) PPO medical plan in the next calendar year.

The Opportunity
Quality Manager, the individual will play a crucial role within Abbott’s Heart Failure organization with primary focus to maintain overall Quality Management System compliance to internal policies, applicable standards and external regulatory requirements.
What You’ll Work On

Acts as a key influential leader, responsible for driving cross-functional audit support and audit readiness initiatives to improve quality systems, and overall organizational compliance to internal/external requirements.

Lead, guide and retain a diverse, highly qualified staff and provide ongoing performance feedback. Set goals which align to business plans and manage the execution of goals through coaching and mentoring. Maintains a safe, enthusiastic, and professional work environment.
Comply with U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, other regulatory requirements, Company policies, operating procedures, processes, and task assignments.

Director of Supplier Quality
BAE Systems, Inc.
Fort Wayne, IN
Job Description
You don’t see it, but it’s there. Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics – from saving emissions in the City of Lights to powering the Mars Rover to protecting the F-35 fighter jet. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. And you can, too. We put our customers first – exemplified by our missions: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®” and “We Innovate For Those Who Move The World®.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of?
Come build your career with BAE Systems at Fort Wayne, IN. Our flexible work environment provides you with a chance to change the world without giving up your personal life. Fort Wayne is centrally located between Indianapolis, Detroit, and Chicago for nearby cultural offerings and professional sports. It is the perfect size city; having enough selections of a big city yet small enough for convenience.
The Successful Candidate
BAE Systems is seeking a Director of Supplier Quality, who will report to the Controls and Avionics Solutions (CAS) Senior Director of Quality and dotted line to the sector Senior Director of Supplier Quality. This role will be accountable for developing, maintaining, and optimizing Supplier Quality assurance strategy, reducing supplier quality risks and ensuring conforming products from the supply base. You will need to build strong relationships with the supply chain, operations, programs, and other quality functions to understand and translate requirements into a robust supplier quality executable plan that prevents disruptions and customer defects. In support of your supplier quality strategy, you will closely partner with the core teams of the sector supplier quality function to ensure the supply base is assessed, qualified, and consistently delivering a quality product. This will be a highly visible and key role to delivering value for the business. This individual must be a self-starting leader who can effectively partner with multiple functional organizations, internally, and suppliers, externally for success.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, communicate and drive a proactive Supplier Quality program for the business
Measure, maintain, analyze and communicate all Supplier Quality metrics, risks, and planned actions, and drive continuous improvements efforts at suppliers for improvement (CAR meetings, SRB, Mitigation meetings, etc.)
Partner with the Supplier Chain function to enforce contract/purchase order requirements, assess and develop suppliers, and drive robust RCCA with suppliers
Investigate, evaluate, and resolve supplier quality problems by analyzing defect trends, issuing SCARs, implementing improvement plans, conducting audits, and leading continuous improvement projects to drive a zero defects mindset
Responsible for developing a collaborative environment with suppliers, engineering, program quality, supplier chain, and operation leaders to resolve supplier issues
Engage/lead in all supply chain discussions to ensure proper selection of sourcing (throughout entire product life cycle) to mitigate risk and reduce overall cost of ownership of the parts
Partner with the sector Supplier Quality team to engage key supplier’s management in a business review process to monitor metrics, identify trends and implement programs to assure demonstrated performance improvements
Manages and develops a high performing team of Supplier Quality Engineers who can build relationships, interpret contractual and product requirements, and assist with flow down to suppliers
Owns and manages the Supplier Quality budget
Required travel of approximately 25%
Required Education, Experience, & Skills
Bachelor’s degree in technical field and 10+ years of experience or 14+ years of experience in lieu of degree
Experience in quality assurance/management within a regulated industry (aerospace, defense, medical), or the overall equivalent
Strong technical knowledge of quality science tools and methodologies, including statistical process control, APQP (PFMEA, Control Plans), and robust root cause analysis
Demonstrated success managing supplier improvements through audits and strong CAPA processes
Strong and demonstrated communication skills (written, verbal, visual) and interpersonal skills (listening and communicating within group working environment).
Organizational skills – can marshal resources to get things done, orchestrate multiple activities at once to accomplish a goal, use matrixed resources effectively and efficiently, and arrange information in a useful manner.
Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
Engineering or Technical Bachelor's Degree
Master’s degree
Strong knowledge of AS9100/AS9102/AS9145
Supply Chain management experience
Lean Six Sigma Greenbelt or Black Belt Certified
ASQ Certification
Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
About BAE Systems, Inc.
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.
Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.

evidence.text:
Quality Control Director
Elanco
Fort Dodge, IA
At Elanco (NYSE: ELAN) – it all starts with animals!
As a global leader in animal health, we are dedicated to innovation and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People.
At Elanco, we pride ourselves on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment. We believe that diversity is the driving force behind innovation, creativity, and overall business success. Here, you’ll be part of a company that values and champions new ways of thinking, work with dynamic individuals, and acquire new skills and experiences that will propel your career to new heights.
Making animals’ lives better makes life better – join our team today!
Your day-to-day will include:
Provide both administrative and technical leadership to Quality Control teams overseeing Chemistry, Virology, Immunochemistry, and other key laboratory functions.
Manage all quality control operations, to ensure full compliance with corporate and regulatory requirements while effectively supporting internal departments and external partners.
Provide quality oversight to the Quality Department and site, ensuring compliance with documentation practices, change management, sample control, laboratory systems, and laboratory investigations.
Support audit responses and ensure timely completion of assigned Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA).
Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and training programs related to sample control and accountability.
Proactively identify and mitigate risks to quality control processes, including analytical chemistry and biochemistry test methods, ensuring their ongoing maintenance, validation, and improvement.
Implement process improvements to maintain a high-performing, efficient laboratory environment.
Oversee quality control investigations involving chemical and immunochemical assays by ensuring employee training, reviewing reports for scientific and regulatory compliance, and facilitating cross-functional root cause analysis and CAPA development.
Supervises 5 subordinates – Manager Quality Control 1.
You have the following technical skills and qualifications:
Requirement – Master’s degree in Biology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biopharmaceuticals, or related, or foreign equivalent plus 3 years post-baccalaureate experience in job offered or any related quality control related job titles.
Relevant experience – Applicants must possess at least 3 years of experience in the following: (1) Working in a regulated pharmaceutical/vaccine manufacturing environment; (2) regulatory requirements, inclusive of cGMP/GLP and ensuring compliance with documentation practices, change management, and sample control; (3) Investigation techniques including providing technical guidance, training, and oversight for testing vaccines in a Vaccine manufacturing environment; (4) Conducting root cause analysis and identifying, developing, and tracking Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), including in support of audit responses; (5) preparation, monitoring, and adherence of departmental budgeting; (6) Lean/5S/six sigma methodologies; (7) laboratory control operations; and (8) Developing and maintaining Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and validating, maintaining, and improving analytical chemistry and biochemistry test methods.
Elanco is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status

evidence.quote: Demonstrated experience leading Quality and Regulatory Compliance programs within the medical device industry.
evidence.text:
Director, Quality & Regulatory
ALKU
Greater Boston
$170,000.00/yr - $200,000.00/yr
Director, Quality & Regulatory
Summary
The Director, Quality and Regulatory will lead the quality team in developing and executing Quality and regulatory operations in line with the Company's mission and vision. The Director will implement and monitor all company quality systems to demonstrate compliance with FDA requirements and applicable global regulations. This position is responsible for providing quality and regulatory guidance for design, development, manufacturing, commercialization, and post-market activities for electromechanical capital systems and consumables. The Director will oversee Quality Assurance, Quality Systems, Regulatory Compliance, inspection readiness, and interactions with regulatory authorities to ensure the organization maintains a state of continuous compliance. This is a hybrid role, expectations are to be in our Woburn, MA office 4 days per week, with flexibility 1 day remote.
Add to Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the company's Quality Management System (QMS) and Regulatory Compliance programs.
Serve as the primary quality representative during regulatory inspections, audits, and interactions with regulatory agencies, including the FDA, notified bodies, auditors, and other applicable authorities.
Develop and execute regulatory strategies supporting product development, product approvals, labeling changes, and post-market requirements.
Ensure compliance with FDA Quality System Regulations (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, Medical Device Reporting (MDR), complaint handling, CAPA, risk management, and applicable international regulations.
Oversee internal and external audit programs, supplier quality management, and inspection readiness initiatives.
Provide guidance regarding regulatory risks, compliance gaps, remediation activities, and quality system improvements.
Lead quality and regulatory review activities related to design controls, verification and validation, software validation, change management, and product lifecycle management.
Ensure effective management of complaints, adverse events, corrective actions, and field actions in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
Establish quality and compliance metrics, monitor organizational performance, and communicate results to executive leadership.
Develop and maintain relationships with regulatory agencies, external auditors, consultants, and industry organizations to stay current on evolving regulatory requirements and industry best practices.
Maintain, prepare, 510K submissions.
Education and Experience
Demonstrated experience leading Quality and Regulatory Compliance programs within the medical device industry.
Strong working knowledge of FDA medical device regulations, including 21 CFR Part 820, Design Controls, CAPA, Complaint Handling, MDR, and Post-Market Surveillance requirements.
Experience supporting FDA inspections, ISO 13485 certification audits, and regulatory submissions.
Proven ability to manage regulatory compliance activities across product development, manufacturing, commercialization, and post-market surveillance.
Experience with risk management methodologies, including ISO 14971, preferred.
RAC (Regulatory Affairs Certification), ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or similar certification preferred.
Additional Accountability Section
Regulatory and Compliance Oversight
Own the company's quality and compliance framework, ensuring ongoing adherence to FDA, ISO, state, federal, and international regulatory requirements.
Identify, assess, and mitigate regulatory risks that may impact business operations, product approvals, or market access.
Report quality and regulatory compliance status, risks, trends, and remediation plans to executive leadership.
Drive a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and inspection readiness throughout the organization.

evidence.quote: A minimum 10-12 years of progressive experience in biologics QC, analytical development, or related CMC functions, including leadership of GMP QC operations in an outsourced environment.
evidence.text:
Senior Director, Quality Control
Crescent Biopharma
Waltham, MA
Crescent Biopharma’s vision is to build a world leading oncology company bringing the next wave of therapies for cancer patients. The Company’s clinical-stage pipeline includes its lead program, a PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibody, as well as novel antibody-drug conjugates. By leveraging multiple modalities and established targets, Crescent aims to rapidly advance potentially transformative therapies as single agents and as part of combination regimens to treat a range of solid tumors. For more information, visit www.crescentbiopharma.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn and X.
We are seeking an experienced Senior Director, Quality Control to join as a key leader within Crescent's Quality organization, responsible for providing strategic and hands-on Quality Control leadership across company’s biologics and ADC programs, and future pipeline growth. Partnering closely with Analytical Sciences, GMP Quality Assurance, CMC/Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs, you will provide phase-appropriate QC oversight from early development through late-stage development and commercialization within a global outsourced testing and manufacturing network. You will ensure reliable release and stability testing while building the QC infrastructure, laboratory network, and operating controls needed to advance programs into Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA submission, and commercial readiness.
Crescent's operating model requires clear, collaborative accountability between Analytical Sciences and QC. Analytical Sciences leads analytical development and performs the primary technical work through method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and PPQ readiness. QC provides oversight and operational input during early development, assumes increasing responsibility for method transfer, validation execution oversight, laboratory readiness, and GMP testing as programs mature, and takes primary ownership of routine QC operations and analytical method lifecycle management following transition to late-stage and commercial operations.
Success in this role requires a collaborative, hands-on leader who understands both analytical development and commercial QC operations, can establish effective governance across internal and external partners, and thrives in a fast-paced biotechnology environment while balancing scientific rigor, compliance, speed, and pragmatism.
\n
Responsibilities
Define and implement Crescent's phase-appropriate QC strategy and operating model across early development, Phase 3, PPQ, regulatory submission, and commercialization, with clear decision rights and handoffs among Analytical Sciences, QC, and GMP QA.
Oversee QC activities for drug substance, drug product, intermediates, finished goods, in-process, release, characterization, and stability testing across the portfolio.
Provide QC oversight and operational requirements during early development while Analytical Sciences leads method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and method maturation through PPQ readiness.
Partner with Analytical Sciences on integrated Phase 3 and PPQ readiness, including method validation and transfer, laboratory qualification, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, stability, sample management, and testing timelines.
Lead QC execution oversight for method transfer, validation, and laboratory readiness; following transition to GMP QC operations, own routine method lifecycle management, performance monitoring, changes, revalidation, transfers, and remediation.
Lead outsourced GMP QC operations, including sample management and testing coordination, and ensure timely, compliant release and stability testing for clinical supply, PPQ, batch disposition, regulatory commitments, and future commercial supply.
Partner with Analytical Sciences, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, and QA on specifications and stability strategy; lead operational implementation, stability execution, data review, trending, and escalation within the QC network.
Establish and oversee reference standard and critical reagent programs, including qualification, bridging, inventory, monitoring, replacement, and lifecycle planning.
Provide technical leadership for OOS, OOT, OOE, atypical results, invalid assays, laboratory deviations, CAPAs, and change controls, ensuring scientifically sound, timely investigations and risk-based escalation.
Lead selection, onboarding, qualification, governance, and performance management of CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including agreements, capacity, metrics, issue management, data integrity, and inspection readiness.
Provide QC input to CMC and regulatory strategies and support IND/IMPD, BLA/MAA, health authority, and inspection activities; ensure commitments are implemented within the laboratory network.
Lead alliance management with business partners on QC matters, including governance, roles and responsibilities, shared testing and release requirements, issue escalation, decision-making, and alignment on development, regulatory, and future commercial priorities.
Establish scalable QC procedures, systems, metrics, budgeting, forecasting, and resource plans; support compliant use of LIMS, stability, analytical data, and trending tools, and build internal QC capability as Crescent advances toward commercialization.
Mentor staff and consultants and foster a culture of scientific rigor, collaboration, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement while staying current with evolving GMP, ICH, compendial, and industry expectations.
Education & Experience
Bachelor's degree in life sciences, analytical sciences, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
A minimum 10-12 years of progressive experience in biologics QC, analytical development, or related CMC functions, including leadership of GMP QC operations in an outsourced environment.
Experience with biologics analytical methods, including cell-based bioassays/potency assays; ADC and other complex biologic modality experience is preferred.
Experience supporting biologics from clinical development through Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA, and commercial readiness; bispecific antibody, ADC, or other complex modality experience is a plus.
Proven experience transitioning methods from development into routine GMP QC use, including qualification, validation, transfer, implementation, performance monitoring, and lifecycle management.
