evidence.quote: Strong commercial record: you have negotiated price, tooling and terms with suppliers and contract manufacturers.
evidence.text:
Senior Manager, Supply Chain (Robot Production)
Genesis
San Carlos , California 
About Genesis
We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
The role
Every part that goes into our robot: who makes it, at what price, on what lead time, to what quality. This is the hands-on role. You build the supplier base for production, develop domestic sources for the sub-systems that need them, and make sure the line never waits on a part. You start with a bill of materials, a design team and a few suppliers; you end with a qualified, dual-sourced supply chain that supports production with our manufacturing partner. You are at our facility, at the partner and at suppliers more than you are at a desk.
What you'll do
Be on the floor: at our facility, at our manufacturing partner and at suppliers; first articles, line-down calls and recoveries are yours.
Build the supplier base: source, qualify and manage suppliers for machined and cast structures, gears and actuators, motors, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two sources for every critical sub-system.
Develop domestic suppliers for the sub-systems that need them, and keep the content records that come with selling into regulated markets.
Run the commercial work day to day: RFQs, should-cost, piece price and tooling negotiation, payment and warranty terms; work with Legal on supplier agreements.
Sit in design reviews from the start: flag long-lead, single-source and high-risk parts before design freeze; bring supplier capability into the design.
Own clear-to-build and the plan: every unit on the schedule has a complete kit before it starts; a rolling plan the line, the partner and the suppliers all see; capacity planning with suppliers ahead of demand; inventory accuracy and safety stock by part class.
Own the BOM in production: cost roll-ups by phase, engineering change control with the design team and Manufacturing Engineering, cost-down from pilot to volume.
Build the supplier quality loop with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality: first article and PPAP where it applies, incoming inspection, supplier scorecards and quarterly reviews, corrective action and recovery.
Run logistics: inbound, between our facility and our partner's, import and export paperwork with Legal, spares and service parts.
Run the systems we have and help stand up the next ones: part numbering, BOM control, MRP; own the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, PPV, inventory).
What we are looking for
You have built a supplier base for a hardware product going into production, not managed or handed to you, and you produce results in weeks, not quarters.
Deep experience with machined and cast metal parts, gears or actuators, motors, PCBAs and harnesses, and the suppliers who make them; you read drawings and GD&T.
You have developed new suppliers in new regions and qualified them to a standard.
Strong commercial record: you have negotiated price, tooling and terms with suppliers and contract manufacturers.
You are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and cost roll-ups, and comfortable with the people who design the product.
8 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or supplier development for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what the systems look like at scale; you have led a small team or are ready to; engineering degree preferred.
Bonus: robotics or automotive; contract manufacturer selection and transition; import and export compliance; APICS or CPSM.
Working Conditions
Office and production environments; travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 30%.
How we work
We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
Limitless ambition.
We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
Relentless urgency.
Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
Type-2 Fun.
Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
Radical transparency.
Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
Multiculturalism
. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
Team over ego.
Help others, share context, and win as a team.
A joyful journey.
We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader
DuPont
Edina, MN
At DuPont, our purpose is to empower the world with essential innovations to thrive. We work on things that matter. Whether it’s providing clean water to more than a billion people on the planet, producing materials that are essential in everyday technology devices from smartphones to electric vehicles, or protecting workers around the world. Discover the many reasons the world’s most talented people are choosing to work at DuPont. Why Join Us | DuPont Careers
Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader
DuPont Water Solutions is seeking a passionate and high-performing individual to lead our reverse osmosis (RO) and ultrafiltration (UF) manufacturing network. The Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader is responsible for leading a global portfolio of (7) manufacturing sites and driving safe, reliable, customer-focused, and cost-effective operations aligned to DuPont’s business strategy. This role provides enterprise manufacturing leadership across a diverse network of sites, partnering closely with business, commercial, supply chain, engineering, quality, EHS, technology, and operational excellence leaders to align manufacturing priorities with customer needs, deliver performance, build capability, maximize value, and enable growth.
This individual will be accountable for establishing and sustaining a lean manufacturing culture that improves every day, reduces waste and variation, strengthens daily management, and develops problem-solving capability at all levels of the organization. Success requires a visible, hands-on leader who can set strategy, drive disciplined execution, inspire global teams, and role model DuPont’s core values of Safety & Respect, Integrity & Accountability, Grow and Improve, and Solve Problems with Customers.
Key Responsibilities
Lead global manufacturing performance: Own performance across the portfolio of RO and UF manufacturing sites, delivering results in safety, quality, delivery, inventory, productivity (cost), compliance, asset reliability, and customer service.
Drive lean manufacturing and operational excellence: Establish and deploy lean manufacturing practices, daily management systems, standard work, visual management, value stream mapping, kaizen, structured problem solving, root cause analysis, and waste elimination across the manufacturing network.
Align manufacturing strategy to business priorities: Develop and execute integrated manufacturing plans that support growth, margin improvement, customer commitments, supply reliability, and long-term competitiveness.
Sponsor and ensure progress of priority projects and investments: Develop priorities for capital investments based on economic models and ensure proper resource allocation to support realization of business strategy. Partner with capital organization and manufacturing technology on developing optionality and strong basic data with cross functional review in support of capital allocation process.
Improve customer experience through end-to-end excellence: Partners closely with commercial, customer service, procurement, logistics and supply chain to ensure end-to-end processes supporting customer expectations around lead time and excellent delivery performance. Sponsor efforts to streamline processes and drive improvements across the order-to-cash process.
Partner with Commercial to align on customer needs and value creation: Work closely with commercial and business leaders to understand customer requirements, market expectations, service priorities, and growth opportunities; translate those needs into manufacturing initiatives that improve reliability, responsiveness, quality, cost competitiveness, and overall customer value.
Build a culture of continuous improvement: Create an environment where leaders and teams challenge the status quo, solve problems at the source in real-time, learn from failures, and continuously improve processes, performance, and ways of working.
Lead through metrics and operating cadence: Use KPIs, bowler metrics, tiered accountability, operating reviews, and data-driven insights to identify performance gaps, prioritize improvement opportunities, develop action plans, execute Kaizens and sustain results.
Develop manufacturing talent and capability: Attract, develop, coach, and retain strong manufacturing leaders and technical talent; build lean capability, succession depth, and engaged shop-floor teams across regions.
Strengthen manufacturing systems and standards: Partner with Operational Excellence, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, and IT/OT teams to standardize best practices, codify tools and processes, and accelerate adoption of scalable manufacturing systems.
Lead change across a global network: Influence and align stakeholders across businesses, regions, functions, and sites. Partner with sites and manufacturing technology to develop the Kaizen funnel and top opportunities across the portfolio and ensure improvements are implemented, sustained, and leveraged to sister sites.
Improve cost, productivity, and asset effectiveness: Drive productivity, yield improvement (reduce cost of poor quality), cycle-time reduction, scrap and waste elimination, energy efficiency, and asset utilization while maintaining strong safety, quality, and compliance standards.
Role model DuPont culture and values: Set the tone through consistent behaviors, decision-making, and communications that reinforce safety, respect, integrity, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer-focused problem solving.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or a related discipline required.
10+ years of progressive manufacturing, operations, engineering, or supply chain leadership experience. Experience leading manufacturing operations in a multi-site or global environment preferred.
Proven track record delivering sustained improvements in safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, asset reliability, and customer performance.
Deep practical experience applying lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, operational excellence, and structured problem-solving methods; Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.
Experience leading significant transformation at manufacturing sites, including culture change, operating system deployment, capability building, and performance management.
Strong financial acumen with the ability to connect manufacturing performance, productivity, and cost actions to business strategy, margin improvement, and enterprise value.
Demonstrated ability to lead in matrixed global organizations and influence across senior leaders, plant teams, commercial partners, functional partners, and business stakeholders.
Strong knowledge of EHS, quality, compliance, process safety, management of change, and operational risk management expectations in manufacturing environments.
Ability and willingness to travel globally to manufacturing sites as business needs require.
Expected Leadership Capabilities
Strategic and enterprise-minded: Understands business strategy, customer needs, commercial priorities, and market dynamics; makes decisions that optimize enterprise value rather than local or functional outcomes alone.
Execution-focused: Translates strategy into clear priorities, operating rhythms, accountability, and measurable results; drives issues to closure with urgency and discipline.
Lean practitioner and teacher: Coaches leaders and teams in lean thinking, daily management, problem solving, standard work, kaizen, and continuous improvement behaviors.
Visible and people-centered: Builds trust on the shop floor, engages teams directly, listens actively, and creates an environment where people are empowered to identify and solve problems.
Change leader: Leads transformation with clarity, resilience, and practical execution; anticipates resistance and ensures new ways of working are embedded and sustained.
Talent builder: Develops strong leaders, builds succession depth, creates growth opportunities, and holds teams accountable for both performance and behaviors.
Collaborative influencer: Partners effectively across Operations, Commercial, Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Technology, HR, and Finance to deliver integrated business outcomes.
Data-driven problem solver: Uses facts, metrics, benchmarking, and structured analysis to identify root causes, prioritize action, and improve performance.
Preferred Experience
Experience leading or operating within a business system or production system-driven organization.
Demonstrated success deploying lean manufacturing practices across multiple sites, regions, or business units.
Experience leading global manufacturing networks that include varied technologies, operating models, customer requirements, and regulatory or compliance expectations.
Experience partnering with commercial and supply chain leaders to connect manufacturing performance to customer value, service reliability, and growth.
Experience using digital tools, automation, analytics, or IT/OT systems to improve manufacturing visibility, productivity, and decision-making.
Location and Travel
Preferred locations are Edina, Minnesota, Midland, MI or Wilmington, Delaware.
30% Global travel to manufacturing sites is expected.

DuPont has job leveling frameworks that help organize roles based on progressive levels of responsibility, proficiency and qualifications. Plant Manager
Forte Opening Solutions
Marshfield, WI
At Forte Opening Solutions, we don't just manufacture doors; we create pathways to possibilities. We empower our employees to shape the future of our industry. Join a team where craftsmanship meets cutting-edge technology, and where your ideas can open new doors. Together, we build not just products, but a culture of excellence, innovation, and collaboration.
We are seeking an experienced Plant Manager with a strong background in particle board or engineered wood panel manufacturing to lead our production facility. This individual will be responsible for the overall safety, operational performance, quality, financial results, and continuous improvement of a high-volume manufacturing operation. The ideal candidate has extensive experience leading continuous manufacturing processes, developing high-performing teams, and optimizing production while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, and environmental compliance.
Responsibilities
Lead all aspects of plant operations, including Safety, Quality, Production, Maintenance, Engineering, Shipping, Environmental, and Continuous Improvement.
Champion a world-class safety culture and ensure full compliance with OSHA, EPA, environmental permitting, and all company safety policies and procedures.
Drive operational excellence using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and other continuous improvement methodologies to improve safety, productivity, yield, uptime, and cost performance.
Lead production of high-quality particle board products by optimizing fiber preparation, drying, blending, forming, pressing, finishing, and packaging operations.
Ensure efficient utilization of raw materials including wood fiber, resin systems, wax, and additives while minimizing waste and maximizing recovery.
Monitor and improve key manufacturing metrics including Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), throughput, yield, press efficiency, uptime, scrap, energy consumption, customer complaints, and on-time delivery.
Develop production schedules that meet customer demand while maximizing plant capacity and operational efficiency.
Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to improve equipment reliability through preventative and predictive maintenance programs.
Build, coach, and develop a high-performing leadership team focused on accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.

Drive capital improvement projects that improve plant capability, automation, safety, efficiency, and cost competitiveness.
Own the plant's operating budget and full P&L responsibility while partnering with Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Corporate Leadership to achieve business objectives.
Analyze operational data to identify trends, eliminate losses, and drive sustainable improvements.
Serve as the plant's primary leader during customer visits, audits, and regulatory inspections.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, Forestry, Wood Products, or a related field preferred.
10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.

Proven success managing plant financial performance and P&L responsibility.

Wood handling and fiber preparation

Mat forming
Hot press operations

Experience managing continuous production systems with a focus on maximizing uptime and throughput.

Strong leadership, coaching, and employee development skills with the ability to build highly engaged teams.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities with a data-driven approach to decision making.

Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Proficient with ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications.

evidence.text:
Vice President of Engineering, Missile R&D
SerenX
Melbourne, FL
About SerenX
SerenX is building the next generation of portable, autonomous defensive missile systems to protect America and our allies. Our mission is to deliver advanced, affordable air defense capabilities at a fraction of the cost and complexity of traditional systems.
We're an institutionally funded defense technology company performing work on U.S. Department of Defense contracts, with a founding team that includes Y Combinator alumni, former Special Operations leaders, and experienced aerospace engineers.
We design, build, fly, test, break, and improve our own hardware. We're looking for the engineering leader who will build the organization around those people.
The Role
We're hiring a Vice President of Engineering, R&D to build SerenX's engineering headquarters in Melbourne, Florida.
Melbourne is not a satellite office. It is where the technology begins, where the systems are engineered and tested, and where we support American and allied operators around the world. The pace we are building for is chalkboard to first operational employment in months, not years, when the hardware, the law, and the end user allow it.
You may have spent years on flight hardware at a place like SpaceX, Blue Origin, L3Harris, or Northrop Grumman. You learned how ambitious hardware gets built, and you learned how a large organization can make that work harder than it needs to be. You want to build something of your own.
The Founder and CTO sets the technology. You lead the people, the execution, and the engineering organization that turn that direction into working, fielded systems. In 2027, working with him, you will grow this team to about 30 people and carry three missile programs at once. You are not inheriting that organization. You get to build it.
Location: Melbourne, FL (On-site)
Employment: Full-time Compensation: $210,000–$255,000 annually + equity
Reports to: Founder & CTO
What You'll Do
Grow a multidisciplinary engineering headquarters across mechanical, electrical, aerospace, flight software, autonomy, integration, prototyping, and flight test.
Hire for ability, integrity, curiosity, and how someone treats the people beside them.
Give every engineer clear ownership, and a path to get better that does not require them to become a manager.
Teach. Know what each person is trying to become, and invest in it.
Make disagreement normal, including from the junior engineer and the technician. Credit goes to the people who did the work.
Carry three missile programs at once, and build leads who can run a piece of that work without you in the room.
Keep the interfaces, the tests, and the field feedback connected.
Keep the pace high without burying the shop in meetings. Enough record to know what flew, what changed, and why.
Bring what the range, the operators, and the defense-services teams learn back into the next design.
Protect the team's time and its standards. Extraordinary effort when the work needs it. Not exhaustion as the normal week.
Stay close enough to the hardware and the range to be useful, and support the people who want to train, travel, and see the work with operators, including overseas.
What We're Looking For
12+ years in aerospace, defense, missiles, autonomous aircraft, or other flight hardware, with real time on integration and test, not only reviews.
5+ years leading engineers across more than one discipline, including hiring, coaching, and developing people into larger roles.
Evidence you have led, or are ready to lead, on the order of 15 to 50 people, and that you can name the leads who made that possible.
You have taken complex hardware from design through integration, test, and use, and you can talk about what broke and what the team learned.
Enough depth in one discipline to be useful beside a senior mechanical or flight-software lead, and the habit of leaving the pencil in their hand.
A record of recruiting and growing engineers who would work for you again.
You can move fast and still stop a test, a design, or a date when the evidence says to.
Willingness to work on-site in Melbourne, Florida and be on the range with the team.
A bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related field, or equivalent depth of engineering and leadership experience.
Particularly Valuable Experience
A director or senior director ready to leave SpaceX, Blue Origin, L3Harris, Northrop Grumman, Collins, Lockheed Martin, Rocket Lab, Anduril, or a smaller shop that actually flies hardware, and build the organization you wish you had worked in.
You have already been the person between a founder, or a chief engineer, and a team.
You have grown a team from a small founding group toward a larger multidisciplinary shop, and developed the leads as you went.
Missiles, interceptors, UAVs, spacecraft, propulsion, or flight test.
Configuration, test readiness, and production discipline put in place without freezing a young program.
Experience with DoD customers, export-controlled technology, or military operational requirements.
An active U.S. Government security clearance. Secret, Top Secret (TS), or TS/SCI is useful. We can sponsor the right person.
Who Thrives Here
You have reached the point where building great engineers matters as much to you as building great machines. You remember what it was like to be young, with an ambitious idea, and to have someone senior who believed in you. You want to be that person for someone else.
You can stand at the bench, listen, and clear the obstacle. You are not trying to prove you are the smartest person in the room. You know the quiet technician who sees a failure nobody else sees can matter as much as the person who drew the system.
You know when to push, when to turn, and when to stop. You can make a hard call without becoming hard on people. You measure your leadership by what your people become able to do, not by how much they still need you.
We move quickly. We take calculated technical risk. We will break expensive hardware when that is how we learn something that matters. We are not building a traditional aerospace bureaucracy, and we are not replacing one with a shop that runs on emergencies and burnout.
How to Stand Out
We care more about the people you have developed, and the hardware you helped deliver, than the number of people who reported to you.
Send three stories. An engineer or a team you taught, and what they can do now that they could not do before. A program you carried through a failed test, a bad date, or a hard stretch, and how the team came through it. A leadership decision you made to protect the team's work or its culture.
Tell us what you would build differently if you got to shape an engineering organization from its early days. We are hiring the person whose old team would follow them to Melbourne.
Export Control & Equal Opportunity
This position involves access to ITAR-controlled defense articles and technical data. Candidates must qualify as a U.S. person under 22 CFR 120.62.
SerenX is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without unlawful discrimination based on any legally protected characteristic.
Learn more: https://serenx.com/careers/vice-president-engineering-rd

Establish annual quality objectives, operating plans, staffing models, capital needs, and improvement roadmaps.
Serve as the senior authority for product quality, QMS effectiveness, release readiness, audit response, and regulatory/customer quality matters.

Working knowledge of design assurance, configuration management, document control, product traceability, first article inspection, MRB, calibration, inspection/test, and supplier-quality management.
Strong command of structured problem solving and corrective action, including 8D, 5 Whys, fishbone analysis, FMEA, CAPA, and verification of effectiveness.
Experience leading customers, registrar, government, or regulatory audits and closing audit findings.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional leaders and make sound risk-based decisions under schedule and delivery pressure.

Experience in a private-equity-backed, high-growth, turnaround, or acquisition-integration environment.
Master’s degree in engineering, operations, quality, or business administration.
Lean/Six Sigma Black Belt certification and demonstrated deployment of measurable improvement programs.
Experience with ERP, MES, QMS, PLM, statistical-analysis, and dashboard tools.

A clear communicator who can explain risk, technical detail, and corrective-action status to operators, engineers, customers, and executives.

Ensure technical processes maintain strict alignment with ISO, aerospace, defense, and medical regulatory standards.

Background in highly regulated sectors (e.g., Aerospace & Defense, Medical Devices, High-Reliability Industrial).

Deputy Head of Production, Connected Warfare
Anduril Industries
Ashville, OH
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Site
Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.
About The Team
The Connected Warfare will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1
,
our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. This team will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for 3 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.
About The Role
As the Connected Warfare Deputy Head of Production, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of defense manufacturing by directly influencing the production of Anduril’s Connected Warfare product line. You will own the short-to-mid-term strategic development and execution of manufacturing operations, driving products to full-rate production. This role requires a dynamic leader who can serve as both a strategic architect and a hands-on executor, leading cross-functional teams to meet aggressive timelines and deliver products of the highest quality for our customers. You will contribute significantly to Anduril's vision of becoming a next-generation aerospace and defense manufacturer.
What You'll Do
Production Ownership & Strategy: Own all production outcomes for the Connected Warfare product line, including ramp plans, headcount, and the standing up of new manufacturing lines. Develop and execute a long-term strategy to rapidly scale production volumes to full-rate production.
Leadership & Team Management: Serve as a strategic leader and tactical do-er, driving all people and resources across production to achieve outcomes. Lead cross-functional teams (including Production, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering) through strong leadership, advocacy, and a consistent on-site presence, holding them accountable to meeting demands, deadlines, and goals.
Operational Excellence: Drive processes and systems needed throughout the product development lifecycle to mature products to full-rate production. Establish and manage the team to key performance indicators (KPIs) for financial, quality, and on-time delivery to optimize manufacturing operations' impact on the business.
Quality & Compliance: Be accountable to AS9100D guidelines and drive a "quality-first" culture across all manufacturing operations.
Process & Technology Advancement: Advise on development and oversee the implementation of digital technologies, from PLM and ERP to our custom MES and QMS systems, that enable our production operations to efficiently scale while meeting customer requirements. Shape corporate tools and processes to support the unique needs of aerospace production.
Required Qualifications
8+ years of proven experience overseeing the production and test of complex electromechanical products.
Strong leadership experience managing large (100+ person) manufacturing teams and directing large cross-functional teams across planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, quality, and production to deliver products of the highest quality.
A strong background in quality assurance, with a track record of driving a "quality-first" culture in a production environment and accountability to standards like AS9100D.
Past success operating in both low-rate prototype and high-rate manufacturing environments, with a proven ability to scale production.
High ownership and the ability to effectively manage multiple large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.
Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.
Ability to work onsite five days a week at our Asheville, OH campus (Arsenal 1).
Preferred Qualifications
Success scaling production operations in a high-complexity manufacturing environment.
Deep experience with the niche supply chains for aerospace and robotics.
Demonstrated experience implementing and leveraging digital manufacturing technologies (PLM, ERP, MES, QMS) to drive efficiency and scale.
US Salary Range
$190,000—$252,000 USD
Benefits
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

Director of Manufacturing Engineering, EW
Anduril Industries
Irvine, CA
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. Anduril's Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) Manufacturing team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for Electromagnetic Warfare. This responsibility spans the full manufacturing value chain — from Design for Manufacturability through full-rate production — including tool design and selection, process creation and optimization, vendor sourcing, quality planning, system integration, and work documentation for the hardware our engineers own.
About The Job
As the Director of Manufacturing Engineering for EW, you will provide strategic oversight and tactical management of manufacturing engineering to support both the development of new products and the scaling of high-volume production. You are charged with ensuring rigorous manufacturing processes are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality defense hardware to our customers. Your leadership will guarantee the fulfillment of manufacturing capacity commitments while driving advancements in tools, automation, and methodologies to improve design, analysis, and execution. This role demands an innovative and adaptable leader who thrives in a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment solving complex manufacturing challenges for electromechanical defense systems.
What You'll Do
Build & Lead the Manufacturing Engineering Team: Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers with deep product knowledge in mechanical, electrical, system integration, and environmental testing. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Drive Manufacturing Strategy & Technology: Develop and implement a long-term manufacturing engineering strategy aligned with Anduril EW's growth objectives. Drive adoption of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance efficiency and scalability across development and high-volume production.
Lead New Product Introduction (NPI): Partner with Design Engineering teams in early to late phases of the development process to ensure seamless transition of new products from design to production. Champion Design for Manufacturability (DfM), Design for Assembly (DfA), and broader DFx principles to de-risk production scaling.
Scale Production Capability: Evaluate, plan, and prioritize supply chain, production, and test optimizations to ensure the value stream can reliably meet production output goals. Develop process flows that break down large, complex electromechanical assemblies into logical subassemblies and sub-processes. Build business cases for vertical integration or supplier diversification where strategic partnerships will accelerate scalability.
Drive Continuous Improvement & Quality: Lead initiatives to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and lower cost across the manufacturing value chain. Drive operational excellence through Kaizen events, RCCA burndowns, component and supplier rationalization, and process standardization. Be a strong partner with Product Quality Engineering to tackle key issues both internally and externally to EW Production.
Own the Manufacturing Value Chain: Take holistic ownership of the manufacturing value chain for EW products, including tool design and selection, vendor sourcing and interaction, quality planning, and work documentation. Contribute to end-customer hardware mechanical or electrical design, including interconnects, board fabrication, and inspection.
Resource & Budget Management: Manage budgets, staffing, and capital equipment planning for the manufacturing engineering organization. Forecast headcount and operational needs to support rapid scaling, including classified production environments.
Define Cross-Functional Workflows: Establish effective collaboration frameworks across Design Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Production teams. Set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and drive rapid project execution.

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing manufacturing engineering teams.

Strong background in make-vs-buy analysis, contract manufacturer management, and supplier development for precision hardware.
Experience managing NPI and scaling production in high-growth environments with condensed timelines.
Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment.
Demonstrated ability to bring up assembly operations for electromechanical assemblies, including PCBA, harness, and RF hardware.
Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.
Proficient with ERP, CAD, PLM, and FRACAS software. Familiarity with quality systems (ISO 9001/AS9100) and MES systems.
Hands-on experience physically manufacturing hardware (assembly, soldering, machining, fabrication, etc.).
Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Region President, the Plant Manager has leadership responsibility for the facility and is the primary official in the Facility. The Plant Manager is key in planning, organizing, and executing the Facility’s day-to-day activities in a safe and proficient manner.
Responsibilities
Facility leadership and general management activities.
P&L responsibility for the Facility through creating and managing budgets that help achieve financial goals.
Develop processes that will maximize stewardship, safety, quality, and productivity.
The Plant Manager will ensure compliance with governing health/safety regulations and procedures.
Assist in recruiting, hiring, retention, and developing of associates. This includes evaluations and performance documentation.
Strategically create and adjust department activities, policies, and procedures to meet or exceed key performance metrics and customer satisfaction goals.
Writes and adjust Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) to ensure standardization throughout network.
Leads Facility teams on Gemba (waste) walks and manages solutions to improve findings
Analyzes, identifies, and proposes action to the solution of problems with the operation of the division departments to increase the effectiveness of the operation.
Ensures all DOT regulations are met in the transportation department
Instrumental in the Development of key metrics and indices to drive improvement within daily, weekly, monthly, and annual results.
Serves as a Facility spokesperson in cases of inquiry, feedback, or requests for special information to facilitate the accurate and precise flow of information.
Aids in the solicitation of new or prospective business by participating in company meetings and any other market activities to foster the company’s recognition within the business community.
Maintain high quality and safety standards by following specifications, local and federal governance, and Sysco’s quality programs (including 3rd party auditing).
Qualifications
Education
Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Engineering or Agriculture preferred or min 10 years’ experience in operational leadership
Experience
Minimum 10 years plant leadership in food production, manufacturing, costing, and distribution experience
Preferred Qualifications
Financial responsibility
Increasing leadership history
Great verbal and written communication skills
Lean Six Sigma or Lean Manufacturing experience
Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, Teams, Access, and Outlook
Experience and understanding of ERP systems
Professional Skills
Deep experience with manufacturing or production processes to include continuous improvement tools
Active Listening: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.
Management of Personnel Resources: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.
Social Perceptiveness: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.
Coordination: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions
Critical Thinking: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.
Reading Comprehension: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.
Oral Comprehension: Listening to and understanding the information and ideas presented through spoken words and sentences.
Written Comprehension: Reading and understanding the information and ideas presented in writing.
Written Expression: Communicating information and ideas in writing so others will understand
Judgment and Decision Making: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.
Negotiation: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.
Complex Problem Solving: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.
Deductive Reasoning: Applying general rules to specific problems to produce answers that make sense.
Problem Sensitivity: Perceiving when something is wrong or is likely to go wrong. It does not involve solving the problem, only recognizing there is a problem.
Fluency of Ideas: Coming up with several ideas about a topic (the number of ideas is important, not their quality, correctness, or creativity).
PHYSICAL DEMANDS
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.
The ability to sit, stand, walk, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and telephone to talk and hear.
The ability to frequently sit and reach with hands and arms.
The ability to occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
WORK CONDITIONS
The above information on this description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by associates within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of associates assigned to this job.
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.
The requirements listed above are representative of knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Must be able to utilize office equipment such as desktop/notebook computers, copiers, printers, scanners, telephones, and calculators.
The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
Must be able to work in various indoor and outdoor climates and driving conditions. This includes Cold and wet manufacturing environments.
Occasional Travel to attend meetings may be required.
NOTICE: The above statements are intended to describe the general nature of the environment and the level of work being performed by this job. This job description in no way states or implies that the duties and responsibilities listed are the only tasks to be performed by the employee in this job. The employee will be required to follow any other instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by his or her supervisor. This job description supersedes prior job descriptions. When duties and responsibilities change and develop the job description will be reviewed and subject to changes of business necessity.

Supplier Quality Program Manager
Tesla
Austin, TX
What To Expect
Tesla’s Supplier Industrialization, Supplier Quality, and Supply Chain Operations team is responsible for component development, part and process qualification activities, quality management, and continuous improvement activities at suppliers and internally.  The Supplier Quality Program Manager role requires effective communication at all levels both with internal and external teams, tracking and reporting of performance to goal, developing systems and teams to manage quality, delivery, cost savings, and on-the-spot critical decision making.  This is truly a cross-functional role that will work with Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Plant Quality groups on priorities across Tesla’s business sectors and the successful candidate will be expected to drive successful, on time project delivery, operate as a self-starter, and take ownership of all areas impacting part quality.
What You'll Do
Support the Supplier Industrialization and Supplier Quality teams in the launch and approval processes for products shipped to Tesla
Work collaboratively with all engineering stakeholders through the various stages of the project: Sourcing, APQP, Testing, and delivery at volume production
Drive vendor partnership working closely with supply chain and purchasing team and ensure alignment on engineering requirements, scope, schedule and cost
Drive requirements and solutions with all internal stakeholders such as Purchasing, Design Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, and Logistics teams for the success of the project
Support analysis teams with problem solving, tracking of open issues, and timely disposition of all defective materials
Track supplier requested change control to ensure timely disposition by internal stake holders, response to suppliers, and implementation
Participate as requested in other project / program activities to support Tesla’s growth and quality strategy
What You'll Bring
Relevant experience in managing multiple tasks with cross-functional teams
Relevant experience in a product development environment - hi-tech, consumer goods or automotive preferred
Excellent analytical and communication skills. Must be able not only collect data and information, but also to analyze, identify and escalate risks, clearly summarize status and key issues as well as recommend next steps
Ability to work independently on multiple tasks and projects with various stakeholders.
Benefits
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
Employee Assistance Program
Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
Tesla Babies program
Commuter benefits
Employee discounts and perks program
Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
, Tesla

evidence.text:
Senior Director of Operational Excellence
Kettle Cuisine
Lynn, MA
The Opportunity
Kettle Cuisine is seeking a transformational Senior
Director of Operational Excellence
to elevate manufacturing performance, strengthen operational discipline, and build a culture of continuous improvement across our U.S. manufacturing network.
Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, this highly visible leadership role will shape and execute our Operational Culture, leadership and plant capabilities, Operational Excellence strategy, establish a scalable manufacturing operating system, and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, efficiency, cost, and profitability.
The ideal leader combines strategic vision with hands-on manufacturing expertise, a proven ability to influence across multiple facilities, and a relentless focus on execution. Success requires more than implementing continuous improvement methodologies—it requires developing leaders, creating ownership at every level, and translating operational opportunities into sustainable business results.
What You'll Lead
Operational Excellence Strategy & Transformation
Develop and execute a network-wide Operational Excellence strategy aligned with business growth and manufacturing priorities.
Design and deploy a standardized manufacturing operating system that strengthens performance visibility, accountability, and operational consistency.
Partner with plant leadership to establish improvement roadmaps, performance expectations, and disciplined execution practices.
Identify and scale best practices across manufacturing locations to accelerate organizational performance.
Manufacturing Performance & Financial Impact
Lead strategic initiatives that improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), throughput, labor productivity, asset utilization, and manufacturing capacity.
Drive sustainable cost reduction through waste elimination, improved material yields, equipment reliability, and manufacturing efficiency.
Partner with Finance and Operations to quantify opportunities, validate savings, and deliver measurable EBITDA improvements.
Establish meaningful performance metrics and management routines that reinforce ownership, accelerate problem-solving, and sustain results.
Continuous Improvement & Operational Discipline
Advance the adoption of our KCOP Continuous Improvement program, and structured problem-solving methodologies.
Strengthen operational consistency through standard work, visual management, root cause analysis, and performance accountability.
Lead cross-functional improvement initiatives that eliminate manufacturing losses and unlock capacity.
Build sustainable systems and capabilities that embed continuous improvement into everyday operations.
Leadership, Culture & Capability Building
Champion a high-performance, merit-based culture grounded in personal accountability, operational ownership, and measurable results.
Coach and influence plant leaders and cross-functional teams to strengthen execution, problem-solving, and change leadership.
Develop organizational capabilities through targeted training, leadership development, and knowledge sharing.
Foster collaboration across Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and Human Resources to accelerate transformation.
What You'll Bring
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
12+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing operations, Operational Excellence, or continuous improvement.
Demonstrated success designing, implementing, and sustaining manufacturing operating systems across multiple facilities.
Experience in food manufacturing, consumer packaged goods (CPG), or comparable high-volume manufacturing environments strongly preferred.
Proven ability to deliver measurable improvements in OEE, productivity, waste reduction, manufacturing costs, and profitability.
Strong command of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and structured continuous improvement methodologies; Black Belt or equivalent certification preferred.
Financial acumen and the ability to connect operational performance to measurable business value.
Exceptional leadership, communication, and influencing skills, with experience driving organizational change across functions and locations.
The Impact You'll Make
This role offers the opportunity to shape the future of manufacturing performance at Kettle Cuisine. As a strategic partner to the COO and plant leadership teams, you will help build a more efficient, accountable, and scalable manufacturing organization, one where continuous improvement is embedded in the culture and operational excellence delivers lasting competitive advantage.

evidence.text:
Plant Manager
Valmont Industries, Inc.
Elkhart, IN
3403 Charlotte Ave Elkhart Indiana 46517-1150
Why Valmont
We’re Here to Move the World Forward.
Valmont impacts millions of people around the world every day, yet they might not realize the many ways. Our technology is helping feed the growing population, supplying the world with more reliable energy and access to renewables, enhancing connectivity in remote and urban locations to create a sustainable future and so much more. Simply put, Valmont is advancing agricultural productivity and reimagining vital infrastructure to make life better.
Join a Fortune 1000 company that respects hard work, honors diversity and invests in our employees as we focus on creating the world of tomorrow, today. We are the modern workforce. Are you ready to move the world forward? Apply now.
A Brief Summary Of This Position
The Plant Manager is accountable for end-to-end operations of the Elkhart plant and for achieving Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) objectives. The incumbent provides leadership, direction, planning, and control across manufacturing, materials/purchasing, production scheduling, and shipping to ensure products are produced safely, meet customer and regulatory requirements, and are delivered complete and on time. This role drives continuous improvement and operational excellence, develops and coaches leaders, and manages budgets and cost controls to optimize productivity, quality performance, and overall plant profitability.
Essential Functions
Ensure that all administrative, supervisory and hourly positions are staffed with the best qualified personnel available.
Drive team engagement through regular coaching, feedback and involvement in day-to-day operations.
Foster an environment of open communication.
Maintain required professional competencies; assess staffing levels and capability; and develop direct reports through training and development opportunities.
Empower all employees to seek and recommend work methods, tools and procedures to improve safety, quality, delivery and cost functions.
Develop, coach, and hold leaders and teams accountable through clear expectations, training, and performance management.
Enforce company policies and procedures in partnership with HR, the Site Controller and operational leadership.
Lead and sustain a continuous improvement culture across all departments.
Own site performance to Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) targets by setting expectations, reviewing results, and driving corrective actions with the Production and Materials team, including:
Safety: OSHA recordable incident rate (TRIR) and VSI leading indicators
Quality: CoPQ: Internal (scrap and rework) and External (customer defects/complaints)
Delivery: SCOT (Ship Complete On Time)
Cost: labor and overhead (burden) performance vs. budget/standard
Cost: operating profit / plant financial performance
Cost/Working Capital: inventory turns and inventory accuracy
Cost: manufacturing expense per earned hour / pcs (TME)
Ensure equipment, processes, and behaviors comply with safety requirements.
Maintain product quality standards and lead ongoing continuous improvement efforts related to quality.
Ensure that production and shipment of product meets or exceeds the conformance and delivery expectations of product users and customers.
Lead cross-functional alignment across sales/marketing, engineering, manufacturing, production control, and off-site operations to achieve SQDC commitments.
Review daily/weekly SQDC performance and implement countermeasures to protect on-time shipment and cost targets.
Communicate plant priorities, performance, and changes to hourly and salaried employees.
Manage inventory to support SCOT while minimizing working capital and obsolescence.
Oversee preventative maintenance systems in an effort to maintain and protect physical corporate assets.
Ensure strong systems are in place and functioning to drive asset reliability.
Lead site-level control activities by communicating expectations and ensuring alignment through a strong partnership with the site Controller.
Recommend improvements to controls, monitor compliance, and provide accountability to senior management.
Required Qualifications of Every Candidate (Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities):
Preferred Bachelors with 7+ years relevant experience or Associates Degree with 9+ years relevant experience or 11+ years of relevant experience
Seven or more years of progressive management experience in a manufacturing environment
Extensive experience with budget and cost management
Working knowledge of all areas of production from material procurement, transformation, through to shipment
Experience using MS Office (PowerPoint, Word, Excel, Outlook)
Ability to travel up to 10%, including overnights
Highly Qualified Candidates Will Also Possess These Qualifications
B.S. in Manufacturing, Business, Technology, or related field is preferred
Master’s Degree
Prior experience as a Plant Manager of a manufacturing facility
Working Environment And Physical Efforts
Work is typically performed in a manufacturing plant environment and the incumbent needs to be able to move about the office and production environments. There is often exposure to conditions such as dust, dirt, heat, fumes, and cold as well as noise levels above 80 decibels. Many aspects of this role are physical and the incumbent has to be able to lift up to 50 lbs. The employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms. The incumbent is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, feel, as well as balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.
Benefits
Valmont offers employees and their families a comprehensive Total Wellbeing benefit package to ensure their individual and family’s overall wellness needs are met. Some offerings are dependent upon the role, work schedule, or location and can include the following:
Healthcare (medical, prescription drugs, dental and vision)
401k retirement plan with company match
Paid time off
Employer paid life insurance
Employer paid short-term and long-term disability including maternity leave
Work Life Support
Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,250 per year
Voluntary programs like tobacco cessation, Type 2 diabetes reversal, one-on-one health coaching, mortgage services and more
Valmont does not discriminate against any employee or applicant in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, genetic information, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by law. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
If you have a disability and require any assistance in filling out the application for employment email EEOCompliance@Valmont.com.

Job Description
Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced, transformational Senior Plant Leader to lead operations at the Jacintoport manufacturing facility in Channelview, Texas. This role oversees a complex aerospace manufacturing environment supporting commercial and military aircraft engine assembly and testing.
The Senior Plant Leader will provide strategic and operational leadership for approximately 290 hourly and salaried employees, driving performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Cash, and People development. The role will build a high-performance culture grounded in Lean principles, accountability, continuous improvement, and strong cross-functional collaboration.
The ideal candidate is a visible, influential leader who develops talent, strengthens execution, and positions the site for sustainable long-term success.
Key Responsibilities

Drive performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Cash, and Productivity.
Advance operational excellence through Lean, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.
Maintain regulatory, environmental, health, safety, and quality compliance.
People & Culture
Lead, coach, and develop site leaders across manufacturing, engineering, quality, and operations.
Build a people-first culture of accountability, engagement, inclusion, and talent development.
Promote open communication, employee involvement, and continuous learning.
Strengthen organizational capability and succession planning for long-term growth.
Strategic Leadership

Identify opportunities to improve productivity, capacity, quality, and effectiveness.
Partner with senior leaders to set priorities that enable sustainable growth.
Use data and metrics to guide decisions, prioritize actions, and improve performance.

Improve cycle time, throughput, quality, and cost competitiveness.
Embed continuous improvement into daily operations, routines, and behaviors.

10+ years of progressive manufacturing or operations leadership experience.
Experience leading managers and large cross-functional teams in a production environment.

Experience leading operational transformation and culture change.
Success managing complex manufacturing operations with large workforce responsibility.
Experience developing and executing long-term operational strategies.

to lead our Bowling Green Packaging facility.

evidence.text:
Associate Manager, Production Control, Semi (Night Shift)
Tesla
Sparks, NV
What To Expect
As an Associate Materials Manager for Production Control, you will be playing a critical role in ensuring the materials team is able to support the production goals of the Semi Factory. You will be asked to work cross-functionally, interfacing with engineering, production, and planning to ensure production goals are being met.
What You'll Do
Tesla people leaders are responsible for a variety of Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) assurance functions, including ensuring their teams’ safety training is current, documenting EHS incidents, proactively correcting workplace hazards in the areas, and empowering others to continuously improve operations
Lead and manage people, projects and resources to optimize production for on-time delivery. Coordinate material input to ensure on time delivery and output schedules, lead in the attainment of increased production efficiency and cycle time reduction and manage the flow of material through the supply base to support on-time delivery performance
Ensure timely and accurate material movements through all inventory areas (receiving, stockroom, floor, and shipping) at the lowest total possible cost while maintaining high inventory accuracy
Provide business analysis and process/system development to optimize transactions and provide required information to the operation in a timely manner to optimize materials management performance, and drive the development and implementation of internal systems and software
Support all planning and production scheduling; inventory control; warehouse operations; logistics integration; production planners and material planners (buyers) for Tesla’s manufacturing plant to ensure minimization of excess/obsolete inventory and increase annual turns and establish and maintain appropriate inventory levels for all products
Support interaction with internal customers and suppliers to obtain feedback, and ensure collaboration between Tesla, other operations, suppliers, and customers result in the development and deployment of supply chain solutions that improve quality, performance and service levels. Provide feedback on suppliers’ performance on overall cost, delivery, and quality
Monitor and drive down overall cost of materials including freight expenses, administration expenses, and cost of materials management
What You'll Bring
Ideal candidate will have 5-7 years of experience working in a manufacturing environment
Expertise in material distribution through the manufacturing process by orchestrating the efficiency of moving material from the warehouse through manufacturing operations in an organized fashion
Proven examples of continuous improvement in efficiency, accuracy, and effectiveness of the materials function within high growth, fast paced, manufacturing environment
Proven success in managing department(s) responsible for some or all aspects of materials control functions
Demonstrated financial understanding of materials and supply chain performance
Strong communication and management skills combined with business analytics, process and system development and change management
, Tesla

evidence.text:
Senior Director, Continuous Improvement
Catalent
Harmans, MD
Senior Director of Continuous Improvement
Position Summary:
100% on-site in Harmans, MD
Catalent’s Baltimore facility is a leading center for biologics development and manufacturing, offering state-of-the-art capabilities in clinical and commercial supply. The site supports a wide range of services, including process development, drug substance manufacturing, and aseptic fill/finish for biologics and advanced therapies. With a strong focus on innovation and quality, the Baltimore location plays a key role in delivering life-changing treatments to patients worldwide. Team members here work in a collaborative environment that values expertise, precision, and continuous improvement, making it an exciting place to contribute to cutting-edge biopharmaceutical solutions.
The Senior Director, Continuous Improvement (C.I.) is the senior transformation leader for the Maryland sites. This role is accountable for building the site operating system, aligning the leadership team around the highest value business priorities, and converting strategy into disciplined execution across safety, quality, delivery, cost, people, and client commitments. This leader is not limited to leading improvement projects. The role functions as an enterprise change leader and Chief of Staff partner to the General Manager, translating site strategy into governance, routines, metrics, accountability, and sustained behavioral change across functions.
The role will lead operational transformation through lean, six sigma, daily management, strategy deployment, problem solving, value stream improvement, digital enablement, and disciplined change management. The emphasis is on building the management system that makes improvement repeatable, measurable, and owned by the business. By strengthening execution and decision making, this role will contribute to Catalent's Patient First philosophy by helping the Maryland sites reliably deliver high quality medicines to clients and patients with speed, compliance, and financial discipline.
The Role:
Serve as the senior site transformation leader, partnering with the General Manager and SLT to define and execute the transformation strategy, governance model, operating cadence, and enterprise-aligned priorities.
Build and sustain a site operating system that integrates strategy deployment, daily management, tiered accountability, visual performance management, KPI ownership, and disciplined execution.
Lead cross-functional transformation initiatives across Manufacturing, Quality, MSAT, Supply Chain, Engineering, Facilities, Finance, and support functions to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, compliance, and customer outcomes.
Translate business objectives into a prioritized portfolio of improvement initiatives with defined ownership, milestones, value realization, risk management, and governance structures.
Act as a strategic Chief of Staff to the General Manager by leading executive reviews, leadership routines, decision forums, communications, and action tracking to accelerate site performance.
Develop and manage a site-wide transformation scorecard, providing a single source of truth for performance metrics, value capture, risk mitigation, and recovery planning.
Drive operational excellence through advanced problem-solving and continuous improvement focused on deviations, right-first-time performance, cycle time, capacity, productivity, inventory optimization, and cost performance.
Coach and develop leaders and teams in Lean, Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, standard work, value stream thinking, daily management, and sustainable change leadership practices.
Embed standardized ways of working, governance processes, accountability mechanisms, and continuous improvement behaviors that deliver lasting organizational impact beyond individual projects.
Lead and develop the Continuous Improvement organization while partnering with global, regional, and Cell & Gene Therapy leadership to align transformation efforts, share best practices, and maximize business results.
Other duties as assigned.
The Candidate:
Bachelor's degree with an emphasis in Life Science, Engineering, Business, Operations, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
A minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience leading operational excellence, transformation, strategy deployment, or business system implementation in complex manufacturing or technical operations.

Anduril Industries
Costa Mesa, California, United States
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril’s fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build collaborative combat aircraft, missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are looking for a Program Director to be part of the leadership team on one of Anduril’s largest production programs. As a Program Director you will lead a significant portion of the product line and will be directly responsible for all elements of cost and schedule performance in assigned area.
ABOUT THE JOB
Strategic Thinking and Decomposition: Ability to understand the long term objectives of the business, successfully develop a winning strategy that maximizes business objectives, and decompose into near term and long term plans.
Execution focused - digging into the details, charting the path and owning the outcome. You will be expected to utilize your technical aptitude in conjunction with your program management, and leadership skills to deliver the best outcome for Anduril and the customer.

Autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from internal engineering, customers, and third party corporate partners to own successful delivery of outcomes on multiple programs simultaneously
Understanding the long term objectives of the business, develop winning strategies that result in meeting Anduril’s business objectives while service the customers needs

Collaborate with senior management to develop and refine the strategic roadmap for Anduril Air Dominance & Strike R&D investments that underpin the success of our programs

Director, Supply Chain and Manufacturing Operations (AI2556)
