Image Sensor Engineer
Tesla
Palo Alto, CA
What To Expect
As an Image Sensor Engineer at Tesla, you will own implementation and industrialization of CMOS image sensors and camera modules—from validated design intent through process freeze, production test, factory ramp, and sustained high-volume manufacturing. Your focus is not research-grade pixel invention; it is making sensors work reliably, repeatably, and cost-effectively at Tesla scale across vehicle programs.
You will translate electro-optical and system requirements into manufacturable module designs, supplier process controls, incoming/EOL test coverage, and line-ready build instructions. You will lead NPI gates, yield and cosmetic defect reduction, second-source and capacity ramps, and field/factory issue closure with CIS vendors, module makers, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain. Expect heavy time on characterization benches, pilot lines, and production floors—not only in the lab.
What You'll Do
Own end-to-end implementation of image sensor and camera-module designs into production: DFM/DFA, stack-up freeze, BOM readiness, build documentation, and release criteria for NPI through HVM
Industrialize sensor/module processes with module manufacturers and internal lines—die attach, wirebond/flip-chip, active alignment, lens/barrel assembly, filter/cover glass, sealing, and cure profiles—driving Cp/Cpk, scrap reduction, and cycle-time targets
Define production test and inspection strategy (wafer/probe correlation where applicable, module EO test, cosmetic AOI, functional/EOL, burn-in or stress screens as required); set guardbands, golden samples, and MSA for factory metrology
Establish and maintain EO and image-quality specs that are factory-executable: QE/response, noise, defective pixels, PRNU, black level, HDR/flicker behavior, multi-camera matching—balanced for perception needs and manufacturing yield
Lead yield, defect, and process excursions: Pareto analysis, DOE on assembly and test, root-cause with FA (optical, electrical, physical), and permanent corrective actions into supplier control plans and Tesla work instructions
Drive automotive-grade qualification and production validation for sensors/modules (TC, THB/HAST, mechanical shock/vibe, solar/UV load, life tests); lock process change management (PCN) and requalification triggers
Partner with Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering, and Quality on line bring-up, takt and capacity models, traceability, and containment playbooks for factory and field escapes
Manage CIS and camera-module supplier industrialization programs: process capability audits, dual-source enablement, cost-down without quality regression, and ramp readiness for new vehicle launches
Resolve implementation issues at the system boundary—thermal, EMI, flex/PCB interface, connector/sealing, contamination, stray light introduced by assembly tolerances—and feed learnings into next-gen designs
Mentor implementation and camera manufacturing engineers; standardize playbooks for sensor NPI, factory metrics dashboards, and cross-program industrialization best practices
What You'll Bring
Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Optics, Physics, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. Industrialization track record outweighs pure research pedigree
8+ years (12+ years preferred) bringing CMOS image sensors and/or camera modules from prototype into high-volume manufacturing—automotive, mobile, industrial machine vision, or similar high-reliability volume products
Proven ownership of camera or imaging-module NPI: process development, equipment/fixture bring-up, production test deployment, yield ramp, and sustained HVM support
Working fluency with CIS electro-optical behavior and failure modes (noise, defectives, thermal dark current, HDR/flicker, packaging stress) sufficient to set specs, debug lines, and challenge vendors—without requiring a pure pixel-design background
Hands-on experience with module assembly processes (active alignment, bonding, sealing, optical stack) and factory quality systems (control plans, FMEA, SPC, 8D, traceability)
Demonstrated ability to define EO/functional production tests, correlate lab-to-line metrology, and use data (Python, JMP, or equivalent) to drive yield and process improvement
Experience with automotive or equivalently rigorous qualification, PCN/change control, and supplier process audits for imaging or precision optoelectronic assemblies
Comfortable operating across Design, Manufacturing, Test, Quality, and Supply Chain; clear communicator who can freeze a process, call a line stop, or present ramp risk to program leadership
Own industrialization strategy across camera platforms, unblock multi-site ramps, dual-source critical sensors/modules, and raise the manufacturing bar for imaging hardware
Bias to the factory floor and supplier lines; willingness to travel to module makers and Tesla manufacturing sites as needed (often 25%+ during ramps)
Benefits
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits

Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
Employee Assistance Program
Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
Tesla Babies program
Commuter benefits
Employee discounts and perks program
Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
Expected Compensation
$132,000 - $240,000/annual salary + cash and stock awards + benefits

evidence.quote: Audit leadership — registrar, customer, and regulatory; you’ve led companies through first-time certification and passed cleanly
evidence.text:
Head of Quality
Foundational Industries
San Francisco Bay Area, CA
Foundational Industries · SF Bay Area · Full-Time
About Foundational
Foundational is building a network of AI-native, autonomous factories for modern contract manufacturing — reshoring critical supply chains so companies can produce high-quality products domestically, quickly, and at competitive cost. Recent breakthroughs in robotics and physical AI have shifted autonomous manufacturing from theoretical to deployable, and we're focused on operationalizing these capabilities at scale during a decisive decade for American industrial leadership.
WHO — Who Thrives Here
At Foundational, we're building with people who want to own something — to do work that matters, in an environment where what you ship is what counts.
The people who thrive here:
Take ownership before they're asked. They see the gap and close it.
Operate with a high degree of judgment. We move fast, and good judgment travels farther than a playbook.
Communicate directly — concise, clear, and candid, especially when stakes are high.
Hold a high bar for themselves first, then for everyone around them.
Are genuinely energized by hard problems in physical, real-world environments. Energized — not just interested.
Stay effective when things are ambiguous, changing, or under pressure. That's the job.
This is a place for people who want to build something that has never existed before and leave a clear mark on it.
MISSION
This person owns the quality system that earns Foundational the right to build — across every vertical we serve and every standard our customers run on. Without it, we don’t pass first audit, we don’t win regulated programs, and our customers can’t ship.
OUTCOMES — What Success Looks Like in 6–12 Months
We track results. Here's what we expect this person to own and deliver:
Stand up a single QMS that serves every vertical Foundational builds in — architected from day one to absorb the toughest standards (AS9100, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, ISO 9001) so layering on additional certifications and customer-specific requirements is a configuration step, not a rebuild.
Own the certification roadmap end-to-end — ISO 9001 as the baseline, then the vertical-specific standards our first programs require (AS9100, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, NADCAP, and others as the customer mix demands) — and pass each audit on the first attempt.
Build supplier quality from zero — qualification, FAIs, PPAP where required, source inspection, and counterfeit-mitigation controls aligned to AS9100 / AS6171.
Establish the operating cadence that keeps quality real on the floor — control plans, FAIs, in-process inspection, NCR/CAPA discipline, MRB, SPC, and the closed-loop feedback that drives yield and cost of poor quality down every quarter.
Define the digital QMS — document control, training records, NCR/CAPA, audit, supplier quality — and partner with engineering so traceability and inspection data are software-native, not paper retrofitted into a database.
SKILLS
Multi-standard QMS architecture — deep fluency in ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485 / FDA QSR (21 CFR 820), and IATF 16949, and a working sense of where they converge, where they don’t, and how additional customer- and vertical-specific standards layer on top
Audit leadership — registrar, customer, and regulatory; you’ve led companies through first-time certification and passed cleanly
Core quality engineering toolkit — APQP/PPAP, FMEA, control plans, MSA, SPC, 8D, root cause and CAPA discipline that actually closes loops
Electronics & precision-manufacturing quality — IPC-A-610 / J-STD-001, FAIs (AS9102), source inspection, dimensional metrology, and special-process accreditation (NADCAP)
Digital QMS & data fluency — comfortable defining the systems and data model (eQMS, traceability, inspection records) that the function runs on, not just operating off a shared drive
COMPETENCIES
These are the behavioral patterns that predict success here — in practice, under pressure.
Accountability
— You own outcomes. If something's off track, you say so and fix it.
Bias for action
— You ship. You iterate. You move toward the hard thing.
Clarity of communication
— Direct and concise, especially when it counts.
Learning agility
— You get up to speed fast in unfamiliar territory.
Resilience
— You stay sharp when things are hard, ambiguous, or moving fast.
High standards
— You raise the bar rather than match it — and hold yourself to it first.
Building from zero
— You can stand up a quality system from scratch — documents, processes, certifications, the team — and run it yourself until there’s a team to hand it off to.
Why Foundational
This is a filter as much as it is an invitation.We're turning reindustrialization from a talking point into an operating reality. The work is hard, the environment is demanding, and the stakes are real. We compensate with base, bonus, and equity to reflect impact, responsibility, and results, with meaningful upside for the people who help build and scale this company.
For those aligned with the mission and motivated by execution at scale, Foundational offers the opportunity to help define one of the most consequential industrial transformations of the next decade.
Compensation
Foundational is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The annual salary range for this role is $180K - $200K . Compensation is determined based on your qualifications and experience. Our total compensation package also includes generous equity in Foundation.
Benefits
Foundation offers the following benefits, subject to applicable eligibility requirements:
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance with HSA and FSA options
Generous paid time off, company holidays, and sick time
Life and Disability Insurance
Pre-tax commuter benefits for transit and parking
Foundational Industries is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Foundational complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We evaluate every candidate on what they can do and who they are.

Waxahachie, TX
About Us
Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.
Our Core Values Are
We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
We never settle by constantly striving for better.
We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.
Benefits
Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:
Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
Tuition Reimbursement
PTO accrual beginning Day 1
Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level.
Job Summary
Director Quality Improvement plans, directs, and coordinates quality and patient safety programs for Baylor Scott and White Health (BSWH). These programs include activities that aim for zero preventable harm and apply safe, timely, effective, efficient, equitable, and patient-centered care. The director develops and implements plans, programs, procedures, and practices to improve patient care quality at BSWH hospitals, clinics, and ambulatory facilities. They review current programs and seek opportunities to resolve clinical quality problems or operational issues. The director develops key metrics for clinical quality and patient safety and directs data testing, trending, forecasting, and reporting to improve health care processes. They ensure clinical performance improvement programs comply with all regulatory, legal, and organizational requirements. The director partners with clinical staff, operations, and other stakeholders to improve processes impacting patient safety and care quality at BSWH.
An entity Director translates and implements strategic plans and goals for their entity. They make final judgments on operational matters and ensure goals are met. They recommend policies and organizational changes for the entity. They plan and execute projects and initiatives that meet annual goals. They plan and direct department operations, handling staffing, processes, budgets, and costs. They manage and advise subordinates to meet schedules, resolve technical problems, and monitor performance. The director oversees a larger, more complex organization or area than a manager. The director may have one or more managers or supervisors reporting to them.
Essential Functions Of The Role
Direct the quality improvement function for assigned area of responsibility for BSWH.
Direct and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including patient safety, infection prevention, nursing, risk management, and medical staff. Works with other stakeholders to promote continuous improvement in quality and patient safety for the assigned area.
Direct, facilitate, and support hospital quality improvement and patient safety committees. These councils provide oversight to ensure high-quality and safe patient care.
Direct and guide process improvement teams and activities using quality and patient safety best practices, improvement tools, and standardization methods.
Direct data monitoring, collection, testing, tracking and trending care processes to ensure safety, effectiveness, and efficiency.
Partner with hospital and system teams to advance health initiatives.
Direct quality improvement analytics, data validation, and data analysis activities. This includes data submission, testing for facility-identified data registries, and ensuring data confidentiality.
Direct the identification of real and potential safety concerns in BSWH facilities. Direct programs like variance reporting, patient safety response, and compliance with state and federal safety regulations.
Partner with clinical and corporate compliance to manage regulatory surveys, certifications, and compliance requirements.

evidence.text:
Product Engineering Manager - Mechanical
Keysight Technologies
Santa Rosa, CA
Overview
Keysight is a mission-critical design enablement partner for organizations solving the world’s most complex engineering challenges. With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Learn more about what we do.
At Keysight, people come together to explore new ideas, challenge what's possible, and advance the technologies defining the future. Here, you'll find opportunities to do your best work, take your career further, and thrive in an award-winning culture. Learn more about our benefits.
Responsibilities
The Precision Meso-scale Technology Center (PMTC) provides the high-precision mechanical solutions that enable Keysight’s industry-leading RF, microwave, mmWave, and 5G/6G solutions in various industries, including AI infrastructure, communications, aerospace & defense, automotive & energy, and semiconductor measurement equipment.
Responsibilities:
PMTC is forming a Product Engineering team, and this role is at our Headquarters in Santa Rosa, CA. The Product Engineering Manager builds and leads a team of Product Engineers, each of whom owns a mechanical product family end-to-end, and is accountable for the team’s results in product-level yield, product quality and customer support across PMTC. We’re looking for an accomplished, hands-on leader who sets a clear direction, develops people, and consistently drives results. The ideal candidate communicates clearly and effectively, partners well with Keysight product lines, operations, process engineering, and cross‑functional engineering teams, and is comfortable facilitating technical discussions and resolving priority conflicts among diverse stakeholders. This role requires sound judgment, strong problem‑solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to make informed decisions in a fast‑paced, dynamic environment while managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines.
The primary responsibilities of a PMTC Product Engineering Manager include:
Team leadership and development
Hire, coach and develop a team of Product Engineers; set clear goals and performance expectations, and assign product families by volume, complexity and yield risk.
Define how Product Engineering works with Process Engineering and Integration Engineering: ownership boundaries, NPI-to-production handoff exit criteria, and escalation paths.
Product-level yield and quality
Own yield and cost-of-poor-quality targets across all product families: first-pass yield, scrap, rework and cost of poor quality. Review top losses with the team, and make sure cross-process RCCA (8D, DMAIC) is led to closure when a failure spans more than one process block.
Ensure product conformance to drawing, GD&T and customer intent (AS9100 / ISO 9001): consistent NCM / MRB disposition, CAR / CAPA closure, ER / waiver and deviation governance, and SPC on critical-to-quality features in partnership with process engineering.
Customer interface and cross-functional leadership
Be the escalation point for Keysight product lines and R&D on quality events, recovery plans and delivery risk. Make sure Product Engineers give early, factual notice when yield or quality will affect delivery.
Partner with operations, process engineering, integration engineering and metrology to prioritize across competing demands and to balance yield recovery, delivery and cost.
Capability and continuous improvement
Build product-family knowledge and capability: critical features, failure modes, approved waivers and lessons learned; set the standard for production OSP qualification.
Provide DFM / inspectability feedback to Keysight R&D on new drawings and revision changes, and report team results and risks to PMTC leadership.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials or Industrial Engineering, or equivalent experience.
8+ years in precision machining or precision mechanical component manufacturing in a product, quality, manufacturing or sustaining engineering role, including 3+ years leading engineers or technical teams.
Proven ability to hire, develop and retain engineers, set priorities, and hold a team accountable for results.
Working command of GD&T and of how machined features are measured (CMM, optical, surface profilometry); you can read a drawing and tell whether the inspection plan can actually prove it.
Hands-on structured problem solving: 8D, RCCA, DMAIC, FMEA; comfortable using yield and SPC data in Excel, Power BI, Minitab or JMP to set priorities.
Customer-facing communication: you have presented quality events, root cause and recovery plans to customers, program managers or senior leaders and kept their confidence.
Ownership mindset. You drive issues across functions to closure and expect the same of your team.
Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Manager, Supplier Industrialization Engineering
Amperesand
San Francisco, CA
Company Overview
Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.
We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.
And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.
We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.
Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.
Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.
Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.
With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.
Join us in building the power foundation of the future!

Team Leadership

Set priorities and performance expectations, provide coaching and clear growth paths for direct reports

Define and standardize playbooks, tools, and processes across the full supplier lifecycle, from qualification through volume ramp
Partner with Supply Chain, Engineering, and Manufacturing leadership to keep supplier readiness aligned with technical requirements and delivery commitments

Bridge global suppliers and internal Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain teams on design alignment, material readiness, and DFM feedback
Maintain portfolio level risk visibility, own global KPI reporting for the SIE function including OTD, first pass yield, and ramp attainment
Provide regular program updates and escalations to Supply Chain leadership

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field, Master’s preferred
Electrical, mechanical, or manufacturing background strongly preferred
10 plus years across engineering, supply chain, and or program management, with 2 plus years in a people management role
Demonstrated success leading supplier industrialization or supplier development in hardware manufacturing, power electronics, energy, or adjacent capital equipment preferred
Track record hiring and developing high performing technical teams in NPI heavy or startup environments
Experience managing globally distributed supplier portfolios across multiple geographies and time zones
Strong communication skills across technical and business audiences, able to work effectively across cultures
Travel Requirement: 30-50% travel required.
Frequent onsite engagement with suppliers to support qualification, process development, issue resolution, and production ramp efforts.
Salary: $170,000-$200,000/annual DOE and location
SF Pay Range
$175,000—$205,000 USD
Please note
: This role requires working on-site 5 days a week. We do not offer hybrid or remote options.
While this role is listed for the location above, we may consider candidates in other locations on a case-by-case basis.
Onsite Collaboration Rationale
Given the highly collaborative and cross-functional nature of hardware, embedded systems, and product development, in-person partnership across engineering and product teams is critical to enabling rapid execution, technical alignment, and successful development outcomes.

Work on next-generation power infrastructure systems
High ownership and visibility

Fast-moving startup environment

evidence.quote: Principal Engineer - Quality Enablement
evidence.text:
Principal Engineer - Quality Enablement
IRIS
Remote
About IRIS
IRIS Software Group is one of the UK's largest privately held software companies, trusted by 100,000+ businesses, schools and accountancy firms to keep their operations running. Our software pays 1 in 6 UK employees, supports over 12,000 schools, and is relied on by 91 of the top 100 UK accountancy firms.
We're a Great Place to Work® certified employer, recognised for our commitment to well-being, inclusion and development - and we're growing fast.
IRIS is in the middle of a step-change in how we build software.
Our Agentic SDLC programme is moving the organisation from tool-assisted engineering to agentic as the default way of working, with a 3x productivity target for FY27. As coding velocity rises, the constraints on quality shift. Manual testing as the dominant model no longer fits and the legacy assumption that parts of our estate "cannot be automated" is being actively disproved by modern AI-assisted tooling.
We're looking for an exceptional Quality Engineering leader to define and drive what quality engineering looks like at IRIS in this new world.
This is a strategic transformation role first, and a delivery role second. You'll set the vision, establish standards, lead organisational change, and build the quality engineering model that supports the next generation of software delivery at IRIS.
The destination is clear: smaller, more specialist quality engineering functions, confident in automation, embedded in pods, owning curated end-to-end capability per product, and over time extending into performance, resilience, and chaos engineering.
Importantly, this is a quality strategy, not a cost exercise. Our focus is on better product quality, faster feedback loops, lower defect leakage, and creating a quality function whose impact compounds rather than scales linearly with engineering output.
What You'll Be Doing:
Quality Engineering Strategy & Transformation
You'll own the global quality engineering strategy across all five Product & Engineering divisions and define the destination model for Quality Engineering across IRIS.
Key responsibilities include:
Own the global quality engineering strategy across all five P&E divisions, including the destination model for the QE function and the transition path to it.
Lead the automation maturity assessment across the estate — baseline current state, including the legacy and on-prem portfolio, and build the evidence base for subsequent decisions.
Support defining and transitioning to the right Eng:QA ratio by pod archetype and divisional context.
Define and own the standards for automated testing across the toolchain: unit, integration, contract, E2E, and AI-generated test coverage. Integrate with the standard PDLC and the agentic workflows being rolled out.
Establish the curated E2E capability suite per product line, what is owned centrally, what sits in pods, and how it is maintained.
Partner with the Director of Agentic SDLC on the QE-specific elements of bootcamp cohorts, agentic workflows for test generation, and the upskilling pathway for manual testers moving toward automation engineering.
Provide the evidence and framing the divisional VPs need to lead the QE workforce conversation in their divisions, supporting the destination model, the upskilling pathway, and the honest position on roles that cannot make the transition.
Support the small specialist Quality Engineering practice that can carry the standards, tooling choices, and harder testing problems that don't belong in any single pod.
Practice Leadership
You'll build influence across a large engineering estate while leading a specialist quality practice.
You'll:
Build and lead a small, senior, specialist central Quality Engineering practice.
Lead the global QE community of practice across approximately 170 QA professionals.
Define development pathways from manual testing to automation engineering and specialist disciplines.
Partner with Engineering VPs to drive capability maturity across divisions.
Develop a Quality Engineering career framework aligned with broader engineering frameworks.
Future-Focused Growth
As the practice matures, you'll help shape several strategic growth areas:
Performance and scalability testing as a first-class discipline.
Resilience and chaos engineering across critical services.
The evolution of IRIS's future Scalability & Resiliency practice and eventual SRE capability.
Quality signals as a product input through the integration of observability, telemetry, and customer experience data.
What We're Looking For
Essential Experience
Experience leading quality engineering at scale in a multi-product, multi-team software organisation. B2B SaaS background strongly preferred.
A track record of moving a QE function from manual-dominant to automation-dominant, not as a theoretical exercise but in an organisation with real legacy, real customer commitments, and real people to bring with you.
Deep working knowledge of modern automated testing across the stack, unit, integration, contract, E2E, performance and of AI-assisted testing where it is genuinely useful versus where it is hype.
Experience supporting and driving specialist QE functions/Team that influences a much larger distributed engineering estate. Comfortable with the team topologies model and the distinction between enabling teams, platform teams, and stream-aligned pods.
Exposure to performance, resilience, or chaos engineering at a meaningful level, enough to credibly grow the role into those areas. Full SRE leadership experience is welcome but not required at hire.
Leadership Style & Approach
We are looking for someone who:
Leads with quality, not headcount. Holds the line on the destination model even when the conversation is uncomfortable.
Is direct and clear, comfortable challenging peers, including the Programme Director and the CTO, with evidence and a point of view.
Builds trust with engineers and QAs on the ground as well as with VPs in the room.
Is comfortable operating with incomplete information and adjusting as evidence builds.
Brings opinions, not just frameworks.
Nice to Have
Experience in regulated or compliance-heavy software environments.
Familiarity with modern agentic engineering tools such as Cursor, Copilot, CodeRabbit and Claude Code.
Experience working within federated operations or platform engineering models.
Why You’ll Love Working Here
Impact:
Your work will influence millions globally.
Growth:
Continuous learning and career development opportunities.
Belonging:
A culture that celebrates diversity and empowers every individual.
Remote Working
Please be advised, permanent remote working, is only available to those living more than 25 miles (in a direct line) from their nearest IRIS office.
Ready to Apply?
Click Apply
- we’re excited to learn about your unique perspective and experience. If you need adjustments during the process, let us know. We’re committed to making this opportunity accessible to everyone.
What to expect from our hiring process
Our process is designed to be fair, transparent and straightforward. Stages vary depending on the role — more senior positions may involve additional steps, and some areas include role-specific assessments such as a technical test or case study — but typically you can expect:
Application review
— we assess your experience and potential
Initial call
— a short conversation to learn about you and share more about the role
Skills assessment
— tailored to the position, e.g. case study, coding challenge or portfolio review
Final interview
— meet the team and explore how you'll make an IMPACT at IRIS
We'll always walk you through the specific stages at the start of the process so you can prepare with confidence.
If you need any adjustments or accommodations during the process, let us know, we’re committed to making this experience accessible for everyone.

items.title: Director / Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement

evidence.quote: You have experience in manufacturing leadership, as a supervisor, manager, or plant manager, and you can speak to how you improved the area you were responsible for.
evidence.text:
Director | Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement
POLYWOOD®
Syracuse, IN
Director | Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement
Syracuse, Indiana | On-Site | Full-Time
Help us build the way POLYWOOD® runs, improves, and grows.
At POLYWOOD®, we have built a strong business on hardworking people and the knowledge they bring to the job every day. As we grow, we have an opportunity to give our teams a common, structured way to solve problems, improve performance, and sustain the gains.
We are hiring a Director, Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement to help us take that next step. This position partners directly with our COO to build and deploy THE POLYWOOD WAY, our management system and operating philosophy, across our manufacturing operations in Syracuse, Indiana, and Roxboro, North Carolina.
You will work alongside site and functional leaders to find the real root cause of problems, lead structured improvements in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team performance, and build the routines that keep those improvements in place.
This is not a role for a scholar who teaches tools from a conference room. It is a hands-on opportunity for a practitioner who has led manufacturing teams, improved the areas they were responsible for, and enjoys helping others become better problem solvers.
Reporting directly to our Chief Operating Officer, you will have the opportunity to shape how POLYWOOD® manages, improves, and grows for years to come.
────────────────────────────────────────
The Work You Will Own
You will help turn THE POLYWOOD WAY into practical routines our teams use every day, from tiered management and daily huddles to standard work, visual management, and structured problem solving.
Your work will connect Quality, Lean, Continuous Improvement, data, and people development. You will put on your safety shoes and safety glasses, seek to understand the process first, and then help the people closest to the work make improvements that last.
────────────────────────────────────────
Where You Will Make an Impact
Partnering with the COO to develop, deploy, and continuously improve THE POLYWOOD WAY across both sites
Strengthening our tiered management system so goals on the floor line up with company goals for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team
Leading setup reduction, value stream mapping, and root cause and countermeasure problem solving with the subject-matter experts who do the work
Leading quality strategy across both sites, including process controls, defect prevention, and corrective and preventive action
Applying structured problem solving beyond the plant floor, to challenges like team member turnover, warranty replacements, downtime, and training
Analyzing operational, quality, and cost data and turning findings into clear priorities for site and executive leaders
Validating the operational and financial results of improvements and building plans to sustain them
Building a network of Continuous Improvement resources and coaching supervisors and site leaders to solve problems on their own
Sharing effective practices between Syracuse and Roxboro and keeping standards consistent
────────────────────────────────────────
What You Bring
You have experience in manufacturing leadership, as a supervisor, manager, or plant manager, and you can speak to how you improved the area you were responsible for.
You have significant experience in manufacturing operations, Operational Excellence, Lean, Continuous Improvement, or Quality. You have personally led improvements, not only taught them, and you can explain tools like setup reduction, value stream mapping, and root cause problem solving in plain language.
You know that improvement starts with data you can trust, and when the data is noisy, you start by understanding the process gaps. You are comfortable influencing across functions and levels, including people who do not report to you.
Most importantly, you are hands-on, practical, and collaborative. You build the skills of others, follow through without unnecessary bureaucracy, and measure success by results that last.
Bonus Points
Experience with tiered management systems and strategic goal deployment
Experience leading improvements across more than one manufacturing site
Experience with Training Within Industry (TWI) or other structured training programs
Experience applying problem solving to turnover, hiring, or other business processes
Experience in extrusion, plastics, or building products manufacturing
────────────────────────────────────────
About Us
At POLYWOOD®, we design and build outdoor furniture that brings people together and stands the test of time. We do this using sustainable materials, including our genuine POLYWOOD® lumber made from recycled plastics. The strength of our products starts with the strength of our people.
Our manufacturing teams in Syracuse, Indiana, and Roxboro, North Carolina, build the products our customers love. THE POLYWOOD WAY will give those teams a common language and a structured way to keep getting better, together.
────────────────────────────────────────
What Makes This Role Special
You will help build something new.
You will shape THE POLYWOOD WAY and how it comes to life across both sites.
You will partner directly with the COO.
You will work closely with a leader who is passionate about building systems and developing people.
Your work will show up in real results.
Your improvements will be visible in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team performance.
You will help people grow.
Many of our leaders have grown up within POLYWOOD®, and you will help them learn new ways of working that can change their careers.
You will join an “All Hands on the Rope” culture.
Improvement is everyone’s job here, from the leadership team to the shop floor.
You will be based in Syracuse with reach across both sites.
This position is on-site in Syracuse, Indiana, at least 80% of the time, with travel to Roxboro, North Carolina, as needed and up to 20% remote flexibility.
────────────────────────────────────────
If you are a hands-on leader who builds systems, develops people, and delivers results that last, we would love to hear from you.
────────────────────────────────────────
POLYWOOD is an equal opportunity employer. POLYWOOD evaluates qualified applicants without regard to characteristics protected by federal, state, or local laws.

evidence.text:
Director of Continuous Improvement
hireneXus
Boston, MA
Location:
North of Boston, MA (on-site)
About The Company
Our client is a growing, private equity-backed food manufacturer producing fresh, ready-to-cook proteins and meal solutions for leading grocery retailers and foodservice customers nationwide. Their products, including hand-crafted, value-added meats combined with fresh vegetables and seasonings, have earned a strong position in the specialty section of the grocery store. The company is growing, and leadership is now investing in operational excellence to support the next phase of that growth.
The Opportunity
This is a newly created role and the company's first dedicated continuous improvement leader. You'll partner closely with plant leadership to build a CI function from the ground up across a 250-person production floor. The operation is high-mix and labor-intensive: much of the product is assembled by hand, the product is perishable, and daily needs change based on customer demand. This is not machine-paced manufacturing, and it calls for someone who knows how to improve operations where people, not equipment, drive output.
Leadership is excited about this role and fully behind it. The right person will have the independence and support to make a real, measurable impact on cost, yield, and how work gets done.
What You'll Do
Lead cost-out initiatives across the plant, with a focus on labor productivity, yield, and waste reduction
Build the KPI and metrics foundation the operation currently lacks, including labor standards, yield tracking, and performance dashboards
Shorten the loop between labor planning and actual results so the team can manage to standard daily
Rethink how manual work is organized and performed, including line layout, staffing models, work methods, and labor standards for high-mix hand assembly
Identify and attack sources of product loss, giveaway, and waste in a perishable environment
Drive structured root cause analysis and make sure fixes stick
Introduce practical Lean and Six Sigma tools and build a CI culture where none exists today
Work hands-on on the floor alongside supervisors and team members, coaching and training as you go
Partner with quality and food safety to make sure improvements support regulatory and customer requirements
Use NetSuite and Power BI to turn operational data into clear, actionable reporting
What We're Looking For
5+ years of continuous improvement, operational excellence, or industrial engineering experience in manufacturing, with progressive leadership responsibility
Proven success improving labor-intensive, high-mix, manual assembly operations. This is the most important requirement.
Food manufacturing experience strongly preferred, especially fresh, perishable, or protein processing environments
Strong working knowledge of Lean and Six Sigma. Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
A track record of building metrics, labor standards, and accountability systems from scratch
Documented cost savings and yield improvements you can speak to in detail
An independent, self-directed style: someone who can assess an operation, set a plan, and execute without a lot of structure around them
A hands-on leader who is comfortable on the production floor and earns credibility with frontline teams
Experience with NetSuite and Power BI, or similar ERP and BI tools
Bilingual in English and Spanish is a strong plus
Must be local to the Greater Boston / North Shore area or willing to relocate. This role is on-site.
Why This Role
Build the CI function from the ground up with real ownership and visible impact
Leadership and investors who are committed to the investment and eager to support it
A growing company with room for advancement as the business scales

evidence.quote:
As the Fort Wayne OEM Director of Manufacturing, you will be a key leadership contributor to the success of the Fort Wayne Manufacturing Hub. Reporting to the Hub Director of Manufacturing, you will provide inspirational leadership in a rapidly growing business and have responsibility for all original equipment manufacturing at the site. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented leader with a proven track record of building and scaling rapidly growing organizations. Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.
Key responsibilities include:

Strategic Product Stream Leadership

  • Own the strategic direction, execution, and performance of the Circuit Card Assembly and Unit Integration factories
  • Serve as the primary point of contact between production and program management

Program Execution

  • Oversee execution of manufacturing in alignment with program schedules
  • Ensure all contractual obligations (cost, schedule, performance) are met or exceeded

Performance Improvement

  • Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma Principles
  • Implement metrics to monitor production performance
  • Initiate corrective actions to resolve production variances, quality escapes, and manufacturing cost variances
Required Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Bachelors degree in Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Operations Management, or related field; equivalent experience considered OR 20 years manufacturing experience with no degree
  • Minimum 10 years experience in production/manufacturing
  • Minimum 6 years experience leading production/manufacturing teams including managing people leaders
  • Proficiency with manufacturing management concepts
  • Proficiency applying Lean Manufacturing principles and visual management tools
Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Proficiency with Oracle ERP
  • Formal Lean or Six Sigma training/certification
  • Minimum 10 years experience leading people leaders of production/manufacturing teams


Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
About BAE Systems, Inc. BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.

Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.

This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

Quality Site Head / Quality Director
No longer accepting applications
Nexus Search
United States
Nexus Search are partnered with a $B revenue Pharma manufacturer to appoint two Site Quality Heads for major sterile injectables manufacturing sites in the US. One site in the Midwest employs 600+ people, and the other with 200+ . Both are scaling on the back of sustained demand and investment.
Each role is the most senior quality leader on site, with full accountability for QA, QC and Quality Systems. The mandate is to strengthen and rebuild the quality function, lead FDA remediation and inspection readiness, and embed a quality culture that supports the site’s next phase of growth.
The role
Full ownership of Quality at a sterile injectables site, across QA, QC, Microbiology, Validation support and Training
Lead FDA inspections and customer audits as the site quality lead, including responses and follow-up
Own remediation and continuous improvement of the quality system, with investigations, deviations, CAPAs and change controls closed robustly and on time
Set and hold the standard for aseptic practice, contamination control and environmental monitoring
Own batch disposition and the authority to release or reject product
Drive supplier and materials quality, including container-closure performance
Build the quality leadership bench and a culture of accountability as the site grows
Report to the Site Head, with a dotted line to the Global Head of Quality
What you will bring
Sterile injectables or aseptic manufacturing quality leadership; this is essential
Current or recent experience as a Site Head of Quality or Quality Director, accountable for both QA and QC at a sterile site
A strong FDA track record, including leading inspections and taking a 483 or Warning Letter through to close-out
Deep knowledge of cGMP, ISO 14644, contamination control and aseptic process validation
The presence to hold the line on quality while partnering closely with operations and commercial leaders

evidence.text:
Sr. Manager of Adventure Products
Rivian
Irvine, CA
About Rivian
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
As a company, we constantly challenge what's possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
Role Summary
As the Senior Manager of Adventure Products, you will lead our Industrial Design Product Team focused on expanding the Rivian experience beyond the vehicle itself. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Exterior Design, you will oversee the end-to-end design strategy and execution across vehicle accessories, off-the-shelf brand partnerships, gear, apparel, lifestyle merchandise, and toys.
This role requires a proven design leader with extensive hands-on production experience and deep factory-level relationships. You will bridge high-level visionary product strategy with rigorous manufacturing execution, ensuring every product meets Rivian's world-class design standards while scaling effectively into mass production.
Responsibilities
Design Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and inspire a high-performing team of industrial designers focused on vehicle accessories, hardgoods, softgoods, lifestyle gear, and toys.
Expand the aesthetic, functional, and strategic design vision for all non-vehicle physical products, maintaining alignment with Rivian's core vehicle design language.
Manage project workflows, design reviews, timelines, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent product programs.
Product Strategy & Range Execution
Vehicle Accessories:
Drive design innovation for internal and customer-facing vehicle accessories (e. g. , gear tunnel components, roof racks, camping gear, cargo management, lighting, and overland equipment).
Toy & Merch Strategy:
Build and execute a cohesive brand merchandise and toy strategy that engages enthusiasts, children, and Rivian owners worldwide.
Off-the-Shelf & Licensing Partnerships:
Evaluate, curate, and direct third-party supplier products and collaborative brand partnerships, ensuring off-the-shelf items are elevated to meet Rivian's premium design standards.
Production, Manufacturing & Factory Engagement
Leverages extensive production experience and direct factory contacts to push concepts through DFM (Design for Manufacturing) into successful mass production.
Work directly on factory floors-both domestically and internationally-to troubleshoot prototyping, tooling, material selection, CMF (Color, Material, Finish), and production challenges.
Collaborate closely with Purchasing, Supply Chain, Hardware Engineering, and Quality teams to ensure design intent, cost targets, and launch schedules are strictly maintained.
Qualifications
To Apply:
Please include a direct link to your portfolio (and any access credentials if password-protected), featuring work in industrial design, softgoods/hardgoods, and production-ready physical products. Experience:
10+ years of professional industrial design experience, with at least 3-5+ years in a team management or leadership capacity.
Production Mastery:
Demonstrated track record of bringing complex physical products from concept through high-volume mass production.
Factory Network & Technical Expertise:
Must-have
established direct relationships and hands-on experience working directly with factories, suppliers, and overseas/domestic manufacturing partners. Proven capability to push factory partners to achieve tight design tolerances and premium finishing.
Category Diversity:
Prior background designing across diverse categories-such as outdoor/adventure gear, automotive accessories, consumer electronics, hardgoods, toys, or technical softgoods-is highly preferred.
Design Excellence:
Exceptional portfolio demonstrating strong ID fundamentals, form development, sketching, 3D CAD modeling, CMF mastery, and user-centered design thinking.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Strong ability to communicate design vision and negotiate technical/budget constraints with engineering, supply chain, and executive stakeholders.
Travel:
Ability to travel domestically and internationally (up to 20-30%) to visit factory partners, suppliers, and testing environments.
Bonus Qualifications
Passion for the outdoors, electric vehicles, overland travel, and adventure culture.
Background in developing both hardgoods (tooling, injection molding, metal fabrication)
and softgoods/textiles.
Pay Disclosure
The salary range for this role is $196,000 - $259,700 for California based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee's position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic.

evidence.text:
Operations Director
Danone
Dallas, TX
About The Job
At Danone, Manufacturing the best products and supplying them to meet demand is a key driver for our plant teams. We are currently looking to hire an Operations Director
based in Dallas, Texas
. The Operations Director will strategically manage manufacturing operations at our state-of-the-art, extra-large beverage production facility. This role partners closely with the Plant Director to oversee all daily production activities, directly manage business unit leaders and drive strategic initiatives, while also fostering a culture of continuous improvement and safety. This role is responsible for ensuring customer orders are produced timely in a cost-effective manner with safety and quality as top priorities.
Key Responsibilities
Lead short- and medium-term production strategies to optimize labor, materials, and workflows.
Drive accountability and cultural change through Danone’s Integrated Work Systems (IWS).
Monitor and improve SQCDMN metrics (Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, Mobilization, Nature).
Provide administrative direction across departments including Production, Packaging, Processing, Planning, and Purchasing.
Manage operational budgets, cost controls, and profit/loss statements.
Partner with HR in a union environment on hiring, performance, and employee relations.
Oversee capital project planning and execution.
Ensure compliance with GMP, FDA, safety, and food quality standards.
Foster a collaborative, ethical, and high-performance culture across teams.
Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential function of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs and ladders, balance; stoop, kneel or crouch; talk and hear. Occasionally required to lift and / or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
Work Environment
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee regularly works near moving mechanical parts and is regularly exposed to wet and/or humid conditions. The employee may be exposed to fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals and may be exposed to loud noises in the plant. The employee occasionally works in high, precarious places and is occasionally exposed to extreme cold, risk of electrical shock and vibration.
Engagement in our Integrated Work Systems
Ensure adherence to plant standards (including but not limited to GMP, AIB, FDA, Quality, Safety, Finance, ISO, Daily Direction Setting, Driving Operational Efficiency). As a fundamental piece of the organization, your responsibility is to participate and own the implementation and deployment of related integrated work systems and corresponding pillars (Leadership foundation, Daily Direction Setting, Driving Operational Efficiency; Autonomous Maintenance; planned Maintenance; Focused Improvement; Education and Training; Environmental, Health and Safety; Quality; Organization; Supply Network; Early Equipment Management) with the objective of owning your space, owning your performance (Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, Mobilization, Nature) and owning your continuous improvement.
Compensation & Benefits
Danone North America additionally offers a performance-based bonus and has a strong benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription Drug Coverage, 401k Plan, Wellness Program, Life Insurance, Tuition Reimbursement, Flexible Time Off, and Paid Parental Bonding Leave, among other benefit plan options.
About You
The ideal candidate will bring a combination of education, experience, and skills that enable them to excel in this position. The following qualifications outline what we’re looking for, including both required and preferred criteria
Education & Experience
A high school diploma or GED is required. A bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, Food Science, or related field is preferred. In lieu of completed degree, a combination of education and work experience will be considered.
10+ years of production management experience in a high-speed food / beverage/ CPG manufacturing environment, required.
2+ years of UHT dairy processing experience (preferred).
Experience in consumer packaging and continuous improvement methodologies (i.e. IWS, Lean, TPM), required.
Experience with budget and cost management, required.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Ability to establish and react to changing priorities
Ability to prioritize plant operations in light of multiple priorities and conflicting demands.
Strong knowledge of GMP’s - to include regulations which govern food products
Knowledge of safety policies and procedures regarding chemicals, equipment/machinery
Excellent negotiation skills. - including an ability to understand sensitive situations.
Strong leadership skills, strong influential ability and strong interpersonal and communication skills required to interact successfully with all levels of plant and organization, as well as to develop and coach teams.
Strong analytical ability and have demonstrated problem solving and decision-making skills; ability to make decisions with limited information and to handle uncertainty and change.
Strong organizational skills, with the ability to schedule activities, and are process-oriented; able to identify process improvements and implement change successfully.
You have ability to support a 24/7 production environment as business needs dictate. Work schedules could include day or night shift schedules, and occasional weekends as business needs dictate.
About us
Danone U.S. is part of Danone North America, a purpose-driven company and an industry leader in the food and beverage category. You’ll work with some of the best-known food and beverage brands in the world. Our strong portfolio of brands includes Activia®, DanActive®, Danimals®, Dannon®, evian®, Follow Your Heart®, Happy Family® Organics, International Delight®, Light + Fit®, Nutricia ®, Oikos®, Silk®, So Delicious® Dairy Free, STōK® Cold Brew Coffee ®, Too Good & Co™, and YoCrunch®.
With approximately 5,000 employees and 13 production locations across the U.S., Danone North America's mission is to bring health through food to as many people as possible.
You’ll be part of one of the largest Certified B Corps™ in the world
, working to make sure our company creates real value for people and the planet. Come join our movement for a healthier world One Planet. One Health BY YOU.
Danone North America is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. It is our policy to give equal employment opportunities to all qualified persons without regard to legally protected characteristics, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state/provincial and/or local law. For our EEO policy statement and your EEO rights under law click here.

Work cross-functionally and collaboratively with other departments to meet Astec’s strategic objectives

Sr Manager - Thermal Processing Equipment
Blue Origin
Los Angeles, CA
Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.
At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.
The Advanced Manufacturing Group's Operations Reliability organization owns reliability of execution across ground systems, GSE, and tooling — including design reliability, asset introduction, and build. As Sr Manager, Thermal Processing Equipment, you will build and lead the function responsible for the full reliability lifecycle of Blue's thermal processing equipment — ovens, furnaces, quench systems, heat-treat, and related thermal assets.
Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Build and lead the Thermal Processing Equipment Reliability function — hire, mentor, and develop reliability and design engineers across the discipline
Own reliability engineering for thermal processing equipment
Own design reliability inputs into new and modified thermal equipment (ovens, furnaces, quench, heat-treat)
Own the asset-introduction for thermal equipment: commissioning, validation, and transition into sustained operations to a defined reliability standard
Partner with Design, Production, Ground Systems Development, Maintenance, and Operations to drive thermal-equipment reliability requirements upstream into design and procurement decisions
Oversee vendor acceptance for thermal equipment builds and refurbishments
Represent thermal equipment reliability in reviews, escalations, and cross-organizational decisions; communicate risk and recommendations to leadership
Direct RCA and corrective action for in-service thermal equipment failures affecting ground systems and GSE
Minimum Qualifications
B.S. in mechanical, thermal, or related engineering discipline, or equivalent experience
7+ years in engineering, manufacturing, or operations in a complex hardware environment, with direct experience on thermal processing equipment (ovens, furnaces, heat-treat, or similar)
3+ years leading engineers or technical teams
Demonstrated experience in reliability engineering methods: FMEA, RCA, criticality analysis, maintainability, reliability requirements development
Experience driving reliability or design inputs across organizational boundaries with internal and external stakeholders
Preferred Qualifications
Aerospace, launch, or other high-reliability operations environments
Experience standing up a new team or function from the ground up
Direct experience with industrial thermal processing equipment: heat-treat furnaces, quench systems, autoclaves, or similar large thermal assets
Reliability certification (ASQ CRE) or formal reliability engineering training
Experience with asset introduction, commissioning, and transition of new hardware into sustained operations
Vendor oversight and acceptance — verifying reliability/quality requirements met before delivery
Base Pay Range for:
CA applicants is $171,093.00 - $239,529.15
Other site ranges may differ
Culture Statement
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
Export Control Regulations
Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Background Check
Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
Benefits
Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.
Equal Employment Opportunity
Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.
Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation
Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com. Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.
