Overview
Englert - Director of Manufacturing
As the Director of Manufacturing, you will lead daily operations and drives sustained performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People. Reporting to the President of Manufacturing, this role partners with Quality, Maintenance, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, Production Planning, and other support functions to achieve plant objectives.
This leader is accountable for production performance, labor productivity, schedule attainment, manufacturing cost, capacity utilization, talent development, and continuous improvement. The role establishes disciplined shop-floor management, develops manufacturing leaders, and builds a culture of accountability, problem solving, teamwork, and operational excellence.
Pay Range: Starting at $130,000 per year with variable comp
Responsibilities
Lead daily manufacturing operations to meet or exceed targets for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People.
Convert forecasts, demand, and business priorities into manufacturing plans, staffing models, capacity requirements, and execution priorities.
Lead, coach, and develop manufacturing managers, supervisors, and frontline leaders with clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
Maintain a disciplined daily management system with shift meetings, production reviews, KPI boards, escalation routines, and corrective-action follow-up.
Monitor manufacturing KPIs including safety performance, schedule attainment, output, labor efficiency, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, productivity, and manufacturing cost.
Ensure production issues and performance gaps are quickly identified, root causes addressed, corrective actions assigned, and results sustained.
Partner with Quality to improve first-pass yield, reduce defects and rework, resolve customer concerns, and strengthen process controls.
Partner with Maintenance to improve equipment reliability, reduce unplanned downtime, strengthen preventive maintenance, and increase asset utilization.
Collaborate with Production Planning and Supply Chain to align schedules, material availability, inventory needs, and customer commitments.
Partner with Engineering and Continuous Improvement to improve productivity, capacity, material flow, ergonomics, quality, and manufacturing cost.
Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement through standard work, 5S/6S, visual management, problem solving, waste elimination, line balancing, and process optimization.
Increase output and capacity utilization while reducing labor hours, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, and operational waste.
Establish, document, train, audit, and sustain standardized work processes and operating procedures.
Develop capacity and labor plans that support current demand, growth initiatives, new products, and changing customer requirements.
Use ERP systems and operational data to analyze performance, identify trends, set priorities, and drive factbased decisions.
Maintain daily, weekly, and monthly reporting that compares results to targets and highlights trends, gaps, and corrective actions.
Support the annual operating plan, manufacturing budget, capital requirements, productivity initiatives, and cost-reduction targets.
Manage manufacturing expenses within budget and deliver year-over-year improvements in labor productivity, conversion cost, scrap, and operational efficiency.
Champion safety by ensuring compliance with standards, participation in safety initiatives, and proactive risk identification and elimination.
Ensure manufacturing operations comply with company policies, regulatory requirements, quality systems, environmental requirements, and operating procedures.
Build succession plans and strengthen the leadership pipeline through coaching, performance management, cross-training, and talent development.
Partner with Human Resources to support hiring, onboarding, training, and retention of manufacturing employees and leaders.
Foster a culture where employees identify problems, recommend improvements, and engage in continuous improvement.
Perform other duties and lead special projects as assigned by the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations.
Qualifications
Key Performance Indicators
Success Will Be Measured By Sustained Improvement In
Safety performance
First-pass yield and internal quality
Customer quality and manufacturing-related complaints
Schedule attainment and on-time completion
Labor productivity and efficiency
Overtime
Scrap and rework
Equipment downtime and capacity utilization
Manufacturing cost
Inventory and material flow
Continuous improvement savings
Employee development, engagement, and retention
Skills, Knowledge, And Abilities
Manufacturing Leadership: Proven ability to lead complex manufacturing operations and deliver results through execution, accountability, and disciplined follow-through.
Operational Excellence: Strong command of manufacturing systems, production management, standard work, capacity planning, labor optimization, and performance management.
Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement: Ability to apply Lean principles and structured problem solving to eliminate waste, improve flow, increase productivity, and reduce cost.
Financial Acumen: Strong understanding of manufacturing cost, labor performance, budgeting, productivity, capital investment, and plant profitability drivers.
Data-Driven Decision Making: Ability to use ERP systems, KPIs, dashboards, and financial data to identify trends, prioritize opportunities, and drive corrective action.
People Leadership: Proven ability to coach, develop, and hold leaders accountable while building a highperformance, respectful, and collaborative culture.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively with Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering, Continuous Improvement, Finance, Human Resources, Sales, and other partners.
Problem Solving: Strong analytical skills with demonstrated use of structured root-cause analysis and corrective-action methods.
Change Leadership: Ability to lead organizational and operational changes while building ownership and accountability across manufacturing.
Shop-Floor Leadership: Hands-on leadership style with consistent floor presence and direct engagement with employees, supervisors, and operations.
Education And Experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business or related field required; equivalent education and significant manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
Minimum 7–10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including at least five years in manufacturing leadership.
Experience managing multi-shift manufacturing operations and leading managers and supervisors.
Strong background in Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, structured problem solving, and performance management.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems and manufacturing data to manage performance and guide operational decisions.
Experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, cost reduction, and operational improvement programs.
Experience working within formal safety and quality management systems.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent practical continuous improvement experience preferred.
MBA, advanced technical degree, or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt preferred.
Bilingual Spanish preffered
Leadership Expectations
The Director of Manufacturing must be a visible shop-floor leader who creates accountability, develops leaders, and prevents recurring operational issues.
The successful leader will establish disciplined operating routines, use data to guide decisions, challenge existing processes, and continuously improve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost.
This role works with the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations and leaders across Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Finance, and Human Resources to achieve site and business objectives.
Physical Requirements
Prolonged standing and walking.
Must be able to lift 50 to 100 pounds and additional weight with assistance.
The physical demands described are representative of those required to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
Benefits
Major Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Flexible Time Off (FTO), Quarterly Bonus, advancement opportunities, and additional perks.

**What To Expect
** In this role, you will support the program lead from feasibility through a process that is feasible for high-speed stamping of laminated segment stators on the Stamping Manufacturing Engineering team.
You will own progressive die design and set die standards, process parameters and quality controls from concept through production launch, working with motor design, tooling and die suppliers. This work makes stator laminations manufacturable at the rate and quality required for Tesla electric drive units.
**What You'll Do
**- Support the program lead from feasibility through making the process feasible for high-speed stamping
- Develop strip layout, material flow and process capability for laminated segment stator stamping
- Own progressive and compound die design for thin-gauge electrical steel, including segment geometry, interlocking and stack bonding
- Set die design standards, tolerancing and tooling specifications for high strokes-per-minute lines
- Work with motor design in concept development so slot profiles, segment interfaces and lamination geometry are manufacturable
- Define and validate feed rate, blankholder force, lubrication and die clearance for thin-gauge electrical steel
- Manage supplier die programs from RFQ and design review through tryout and production approval
- Lead PFMEA and DFMEA and put countermeasures into die design and process controls
- Define quality plans for geometry, burr height, flatness and interlock integrity, with SPC at high volume
- Specify presses, coil handling and in-line inspection, and support tryout, commissioning and ramp at suppliers and Tesla sites
**What You'll Bring
**- Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering or equivalent experience
- 5 years of relevant stamping experience, or 3 years with a degree
- Progressive die design for high-speed stamping, including strip layout, station sequencing and components such as punches, dies, pilots, lifters and cams
- Electrical steel stamping, including thin-gauge behavior, springback and burr control
- Stator lamination or laminated core manufacturing, including segment geometry, interlocking and stack assembly
- High-speed press operations at 200 strokes per minute or above, in cluding press selection, dynamic load and coil feed integration
- GD&T for tooling and lamination drawings, PFMEA, DFMEA and die CAD in CATIA, NX or equivalent
- Preferred: traction motor segment stators, self-bonding or mechanical interlock, in-die sensing and forming simulation in AutoForm, Dynaform or Simufact
- Essential physical demands: work on the factory floor around stamping equipment, support die tryouts and travel up to 25% to suppliers and Tesla sites

### Lisa DiOrazio MS SHRM-CP
The Corporate Director of Operations will initially focus on supporting expansion and establishing stable, reliable plant operations. This leader will work closely with plant leadership to strengthen production execution, equipment readiness, staffing alignment, and accountability while ensuring capacity supports customer demand.
The Director will connect Operations with Engineering, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Planning, Quality, Safety, EHS, Finance, HR, and IT to improve coordination, resolve operational barriers, and deliver sustainable performance improvements.
Key Responsibilities
• Lead an integrated expansion and stabilization plan with clear milestones, owners,
resource requirements, and measurable outcomes.
• Coordinate equipment commissioning, production readiness, employee training, and capacity
ramp-up with Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, and plant leadership.
• Align production capacity, labor coverage, materials, and inventory plans with customer
requirements.
• Establish consistent operating reviews that track performance, address risks, and ensure timely
follow-through.
• Partner with plant managers to improve throughput, schedule attainment, equipment reliability,
yield, waste, and labor productivity.
• Strengthen coordination across functions so project decisions reflect operational, financial,
staffing, and customer impacts.
• Develop common operating practices and performance measures across manufacturing
locations.
• Coach plant leadership and supervisors to strengthen communication, problem-solving, and
accountability.
• Support capital planning, operational budgeting, and ERP adoption through clearly defined
business requirements and plant readiness.
• Ensure operational improvements support established safety, quality, and employee safety
standards.
Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business, or a related field, or
equivalent relevant experience.
• Ten or more years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including plant or multisite responsibility.
• Demonstrated success with plant expansions, production ramp-ups, operational stabilization, and
continuous improvement.
• Strong working knowledge of production planning, equipment reliability, operating costs, and
manufacturing performance measures.
• Ability to lead across functions, develop managers, and turn improvement plans into sustained
results.

Delta Electronics is a global innovator at the forefront of technologies powering the future. Since 1971, we’ve been leading the way in high-efficiency power and thermal management solutions.
Today, we’re driving transformation across industries with smart, sustainable systems that enable everything from AI, industrial automation, and data centers to EV charging, renewable energy, and intelligent buildings.
**Role Summary
** The Operations Excellence Director for Field Service will lead continuous improvement and operational governance across the company’s AM Region service organization. Reporting to the Sr.
Director of Services, this role owns cross‑functional programs that improve Quality and Safety, optimize Spare Parts performance, strengthen Authorized Service Provider (ASP) networks, elevate Business Management discipline, and maximize Field Force Efficiency.
The Director will translate strategy into measurable operational improvements that protect margin, increase customer satisfaction, and scale the service business as a profit center.
**Key Responsibilities
**
* Quality and Safety
* Develop and maintain regional quality and safety standards, policies, and audit programs
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action programs for recurring failures and safety incidents
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives (Lean, Six Sigma) to reduce defects, rework, and safety events
* Partner with Product Quality, R&D, and Regulatory to close the loop on field feedback
* Spare Parts
* Own spare parts strategy: forecasting, inventory targets, SKU rationalization, and obsolescence management
* Implement metrics and processes to improve parts availability, reduce lead times, and lower carrying costs
* Coordinate with Supply Chain, Procurement, and Logistics to optimize regional replenishment and local stocking models
* Define serviceable parts policies and pricing guidelines to protect service margin
* Authorized Service Provider Management
* Build and govern the ASP program: selection criteria, onboarding, certification, performance management, and commercial terms
* Create ASP scorecards and remediation plans; run regular business reviews
* Design incentives and training programs to align ASP behavior with company standards and customer outcomes
* Business Management
* Establish and enforce service operating model, governance, and financial controls across the Americas
* Drive service P&L discipline: margin improvement, cost-to-serve optimization, and revenue growth levers
* Standardize reporting, forecasting, and KPI dashboards for leadership and regional managers
* Lead cross functional initiatives (pricing, warranty policy, contract terms) to improve predictability and profitability
* Field Force Efficiency
* Improve technician productivity through scheduling optimization, skills alignment, remote support, and first time fix initiatives
* Deploy workforce management best practices and tools (capacity planning, utilization, travel optimization)
* Champion digital enablement (mobile tools, knowledge bases, remote diagnostics) to reduce on site time and repeat visits
* Set targets and run programs to improve response times, utilization, and technician retention
**Success Metrics and KPIs
**
* Safety: Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) and severity metrics
* Quality: Repeat visit rate; first‑time fix rate (FTFR); warranty claim rate.
* Spare Parts: Parts availability; inventory turns; stock‑out frequency; parts cost as % of service revenue
* ASP: ASP compliance score; ASP NPS; percentage of work performed by certified ASPs
* Business: Service gross margin; cost‑to‑serve; service revenue growth vs. plan
